# OHMNI PCB Component 3D Library Specification (PCB_COMPONENT_3D_LIBRARY_SPEC)

**Document status: first research pass, 180 entries.** complete: 96, partial: 84, research_required: 0.

Read this before implementing:

1. Treat each entry's `status` and `confidence` as authoritative. `complete` means key dimensions have a cited source at confidence M or better. `partial` entries are usable for a first implementation using the stated OHMNI defaults, but contain values tagged UNCERTAIN, RECALLED_UNVERIFIED, or RESEARCH_REQUIRED that must not be presented as sourced.
2. Sources were read through a text-extraction fetch tool, mostly without visual inspection of drawings. Many manufacturer PDFs, standards (JEDEC, IEC, EIA, USB-IF, HDMI) and some distributors were not accessible, and the web-search budget ran out during the last research wave. Where a standard is mentioned it is cited only as printed in a manufacturer document that was opened.
3. The master table below lists every entry with its status. The Open Research Gaps table lists everything that still needs a second pass (recommended before final geometry sign-off for the entries marked partial/research_required).
4. Each group file begins with the package-family sections (shared geometry and member tables). Entries document deltas and member-specific numbers.
5. Proposed additions found during research (IDs OHM-201 and up) are at the end of each group part and are not yet part of the 180-item backlog.

---


Source of truth for OHMNI's component 3D modeling pipeline. Written for Codex (implementation agent). This document specifies PHYSICAL geometry, PCB interface, materials, and appearance. It does not contain implementation code.

---

## 1. Purpose

1. Give an implementation agent enough researched, cited physical data to build every library component without further web research.
2. Establish one shared coordinate system, origin rule, orientation rule, material palette, and naming scheme so that all models are mutually consistent.
3. Expose shared geometry (package families and generators) so that ~180 logical library entries are built from a much smaller set of procedural generators.

Scope rule: electronic function is mentioned only when it changes physical appearance (polarity, markings, size class).

---

## 2. Coordinate System

- Right-handed Cartesian. PCB plane = XY. Height axis = +Z (away from board, "up").
- Top-side mounting is canonical. Bottom-side placement is produced by mirroring Z about Z=0 and flipping X (a board-side transform), never by separate models.
- Rotation 0 deg is defined per entry in the YAML `orientation` block and is the orientation used by the footprint at 0 deg rotation in the OHMNI editor.
- View convention: "top view" means looking down the -Z direction at the board with +X to the right and +Y up on screen.

## 3. Unit Conventions

- Canonical unit: millimeter (mm). All dimensions in this spec are mm unless suffixed.
- Angles in degrees. Draft angles, chamfers, and bends are in degrees.
- Imperial codes (0603 etc.) are NAMES, not dimensions. Where an imperial/metric ambiguity exists, both codes are stated (Section 12).
- Inch-based pitches are written in mm with the inch value in parentheses on first mention (2.54 mm (0.100 in)).
- Dimension precision: report the precision the source supports. Do not pad digits. Defaults chosen by OHMNI are stated to at most 2 decimals unless the source gives more.

## 4. Origin Conventions (ONE system)

**Footprint-Centroid Origin (FCO).**

- Origin XY = center of the axis-aligned bounding box of the electrical/mechanical pad-or-hole pattern: all signal pins/pads/holes plus any mounting holes, shield pins, and thermal/exposed pads that belong to the footprint. It is NOT the body center.
- Origin Z = top surface of the PCB (the board-top seating plane). Body underside, standoffs, and SMD terminal undersides sit at Z >= 0. A component seated flush has its lowest body face at Z = 0 (plus the entry's `standoff` where it applies).
- Through-hole lead tails extend to negative Z. Default tail bottom: `Z = -(board_thickness + 1.0)` with `board_thickness` default 1.6 mm, so default -2.6 mm. LOD0 may omit tails.
- Where the body is not centered on the pad pattern (connectors that overhang the board edge, right-angle parts, off-center cans), the entry states `body_offset_mm` = (x, y) of the body bounding-box center relative to the origin. This replaces any alternative origin.
- Each entry states the XY coordinates of pin 1 relative to the origin.

Rationale: FCO makes footprint-to-model alignment trivial for a footprint generator (the pad pattern is centered at 0,0, and for most SMD parts the body is too). Pin-1 origin (the KiCad THT convention) is used by many libraries, but it makes variable pin-count generators shift the body as N changes. Entries therefore record pin-1 coordinates explicitly so an importer can re-origin if needed.

## 5. PCB Plane and Seating Conventions

- Board nominal thickness 1.6 mm for model purposes (parameter `board_thickness_mm`). Board surface is Z=0, board material occupies Z in [-board_thickness, 0].
- SMD terminal underside at Z=0 (solder paste/fillet thickness is ignored, ~0.05-0.1 mm; not modeled except where an entry says otherwise).
- THT bodies rest on the board unless an entry specifies a standoff (spacer feet, bent-lead stand-offs, kinked leads).
- Connectors that overhang the board edge: body extends beyond the board outline in the documented direction; the entry gives overhang distance.
- Solder fillets and pads are NOT part of the component model. The footprint/pad layer is separate.

## 6. Orientation Conventions

At rotation 0 (top view, +X right, +Y up):

| Package type | Rule |
|---|---|
| 2-terminal chip/axial/radial | Terminals lie on the X axis. Terminal 1 at -X. For polarized parts, the entry states whether terminal 1 is anode/cathode/plus/minus and flags that EDA libraries differ. |
| Dual-row (DIP, SOIC, TSSOP, SSOP, MSOP, DFN/SON with two rows; NOT the SOT-23 family, which follows the 3-lead rule below) | Rows are parallel to Y; row spacing is measured along X. Pin 1 at the top-left corner (-X, +Y). Pins count down the left row (-Y direction), then up the right row (+Y direction): counter-clockwise numbering viewed from top. |
| 3-lead transistors (TO-92, SOT-89, SOT-223, TO-126, TO-220, TO-247, DPAK, D2PAK) | Leads in a row along X, pin 1 at -X. Tabbed power packages: tab on the +Y side of the body by default; leads exit toward -Y (SMD) or go down into the board (THT vertical). Each entry states exact coordinates. SOT-23 family: pins 1-2 on the -Y side (pin 1 at -X), remaining pins on the +Y side, per JEDEC-style numbering (counter-clockwise from top view); the entry states exact coordinates and the source. |
| Quad (QFP, QFN, PLCC, WLCSP/BGA grid) | Pin 1 at top-left; numbering counter-clockwise (QFP/QFN/PLCC: down the left side, then bottom side left-to-right, then up the right side, then top right-to-left). BGA: pin-1 corner is top-left, ball names alphanumeric (A1 at top-left, letters increase downward (-Y), numbers increase to the right (+X)). |
| Single-row headers/terminals | Row runs along Y. Pin 1 at the +Y end, numbering toward -Y. |
| Dual-row headers (2xN) | Pairs run along X. Row-wise numbering: odd pins on -X column, even pins on +X column, pin 1 at (-X, +Y), pairs descending in -Y. (DIP-style column-wise numbering is NOT used for headers.) |
| Connectors with a mating face (USB, HDMI, RJ45, audio, DC jack, SD) | Mating face points toward +Y by default for board-edge-style connectors. Entry states the mating direction. |
| Polarity/pin-1 marks | Always documented per entry, including which corner/side. |

Where a datasheet/standard gives a different pin-1 location, the entry follows the standard and records the delta explicitly.

## 7. Material Conventions

Materials are named tokens. Codex maps tokens to the renderer's PBR parameters. Color values are OHMNI default appearance values in sRGB hex (they are visual defaults, not measured research claims).

| Token | Use | Base color | Roughness | Metallic | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MAT_EPOXY_BLACK | IC molding compound, tantalum/diode bodies | #1B1B1D | 0.55 | 0 | Slightly matte, a laser-mark region lightens to #6E6E70 |
| MAT_EPOXY_DARKGRAY | Alternate IC body | #2E2F33 | 0.55 | 0 | |
| MAT_CERAMIC_ALUMINA_WHITE | Resistor chip substrate (underside), cement resistor | #E9E6DC | 0.7 | 0 | |
| MAT_RESISTOR_COAT_BLACK | Thick-film chip resistor top face | #17171A | 0.4 | 0 | Often glossy black overglaze |
| MAT_MLCC_BROWN | Ceramic chip capacitor body, X7R/X5R style | #8C6A45 | 0.6 | 0 | Tan to brown |
| MAT_MLCC_GRAY | Ceramic chip capacitor body, NP0/C0G style | #8F8F88 | 0.6 | 0 | |
| MAT_TIN_BRIGHT | Tin-plated terminals/leads | #BFC1C4 | 0.35 | 1.0 | |
| MAT_TIN_MATTE | Matte tin leads | #A9ACAF | 0.5 | 1.0 | |
| MAT_NICKEL | Nickel-plated shells, tabs | #A8A9AD | 0.3 | 1.0 | |
| MAT_GOLD | Gold-plated contacts | #D4A84B | 0.25 | 1.0 | |
| MAT_COPPER | Exposed copper | #B87333 | 0.4 | 1.0 | |
| MAT_STEEL_STAINLESS | Shells, screws | #B5B7B9 | 0.3 | 1.0 | |
| MAT_ALUMINUM_ANODIZED_BLACK | Heatsink-like parts | #222326 | 0.5 | 0.9 | |
| MAT_ALUMINUM_CAN | Electrolytic can sleeve base | #BEBFC2 | 0.35 | 1.0 | Usually covered by a printed sleeve |
| MAT_PVC_SLEEVE_BLUE / _BLACK / _GREEN / _RED | Electrolytic sleeves | varies | 0.45 | 0 | Entry gives color |
| MAT_PLASTIC_BLACK | Connector housings, headers | #151517 | 0.5 | 0 | |
| MAT_PLASTIC_WHITE | White connector housings | #EDEDE8 | 0.5 | 0 | |
| MAT_PLASTIC_NATURAL | Natural nylon/beige housings | #DCCFB0 | 0.5 | 0 | |
| MAT_PLASTIC_CLEAR | Clear LED lens (water-clear) | #FFFFFF | 0.05 | 0 | alpha 0.15-0.4 |
| MAT_PLASTIC_DIFFUSED | Diffused (tinted) LED lens | LED color | 0.2 | 0 | translucent |
| MAT_GLASS | Glass windows | #CFE0E8 | 0.05 | 0 | alpha 0.2 |
| MAT_FERRITE_DARK | Ferrite cores | #2B2B2D | 0.6 | 0 | |
| MAT_FR4_GREEN / _BLACK / _BLUE / _RED | Module PCBs | varies | 0.5 | 0 | |
| MAT_SILKSCREEN_WHITE | Printed markings | #F2F2F0 | 0.7 | 0 | |
| MAT_SOLDER_BALL | BGA/WLCSP balls | #B7B9BC | 0.35 | 1.0 | |

Do not model invisible internal layers (die, wire bonds, electrodes inside MLCC bodies) unless an entry says they affect the visible look.

## 8. Color Conventions

- Body/terminal colors are given as ranges ("black to dark gray") and a single OHMNI default token.
- LED color: the lens/emitter color is a parameter (`led_color`); the entry lists the typical visual color for each standard color (red, green, blue, yellow, white, amber).
- Markings (text, polarity bands, pin-1 dots) are specified as decals separate from the geometry. Decals are optional at LOD0.
- Resistor color-band decode tables are not repeated per entry; the entry states the band count and layout only.

## 9. Dimensional Confidence System

Every dimension in an entry carries:

```
<name>:
  default: <OHMNI deterministic default, mm>
  min: <lowest credible value>      # optional
  max: <highest credible value>     # optional
  basis: STANDARD | MFR_DRAWING | MFR_DATASHEET | CONSENSUS | DERIVED | UNCERTAIN
  confidence: H | M | L
```

- **STANDARD**: from JEDEC/IEC/EIA/EIAJ/other standard text or a manufacturer document that explicitly reproduces the standard outline (cite which).
- **MFR_DRAWING / MFR_DATASHEET**: from a specific manufacturer mechanical drawing/datasheet (cite part number).
- **CONSENSUS**: agreement across 3 or more independent manufacturer documents (cite them).
- **DERIVED**: computed from other cited dimensions (state the formula).
- **UNCERTAIN**: the value is a placeholder; confidence must be L, and the entry must carry a RESEARCH_REQUIRED note.

Confidence levels:

- **H**: standard or primary drawing directly supports the value.
- **M**: single manufacturer or distributor-hosted drawing, or consensus of datasheets without a standard.
- **L**: indirect or conflicting sources.

Source tiers (use in Sources sections):

- **S1**: JEDEC, IEC, EIA, EIAJ, IPC, other standards bodies
- **S2**: official manufacturer package drawing/mechanical outline
- **S3**: official manufacturer datasheet
- **S4**: distributor-hosted manufacturer documentation
- **S5**: reputable engineering reference

`RESEARCH_REQUIRED` marks any value that could not be established. Nothing is invented.

## 10. LOD Definitions

Triangle budgets are guidelines for the generator authors, not research data.

- **LOD0** (silhouette, large scenes): the convex-ish outline of body + terminals as primitives. No markings, no chamfers except those that change the silhouette substantially. Guideline: < 100 triangles for simple parts; leads of high-pin-count parts may be merged into a single band/strip.
- **LOD1** (normal OHMNI editor view): recognizable geometry. All individually visible terminals/leads, main chamfers/bevels, tab/hole features, polarity features, lenses, shells. Markings as decals. Guideline: ~200-3000 triangles.
- **LOD2** (close-up/hero): LOD1 plus fillets/radii, lead bend radii, mold-draft, ejector/vent features, shell seams and tabs, knurling, gold contacts inside connectors, printed-sleeve detail. Guideline: up to ~20k triangles. Microgeometry that cannot be seen at normal close-up zoom (inner contact springs unseen from outside, die/wire bonds) is excluded.

Each entry states what appears at each level.

## 11. Package Reuse Strategy

Three layers:

1. **Generator (GEN-*)**: a procedural routine parameterized by dimensions (e.g., GEN-CHIP_2T, GEN-DUAL_GULLWING, GEN-QUAD_GULLWING, GEN-QFN, GEN-DIP, GEN-AXIAL, GEN-RADIAL_CAN, GEN-HEADER, GEN-MODULAR_JACK, ...).
2. **Package family (PKG-*)**: one physical package definition, with a size table for its members (e.g., PKG-CHIP2T has 01005...2512; PKG-SOIC has SOIC-8/14/16/20). A family owns the shared geometry description and the member dimension table.
3. **Library component (OHM-NNN)**: a logical entry in the OHMNI library. It instantiates a package-family member (class B), a parameter variant (class C), unique geometry (class A), or an assembly (class D). Electronic function (resistor vs MLCC vs inductor) changes materials/colors/markings, not the package outline.

Classification (every entry carries one):

- **A**: unique geometry (no reuse beyond itself, or reused only trivially)
- **B**: package-family instance (a member row of an existing family)
- **C**: parametric variant (a family with an extra parameter or modifier, for example a current-sense resistor as a wide-terminal chip)
- **D**: module/assembly (multiple sub-bodies, for example LCD module = PCB + glass + bezel + header; pluggable terminal block = header + plug)

Where a backlog entry is a **function** rather than a package (Schottky, Zener, TVS diode; TCXO; transistor/regulator), the entry maps to a concrete package family and states the default package chosen as the OHMNI representative.

Package families are owned by exactly one section file (see Manifest). Other entries reference the family by ID and only document their deltas. Entries must NOT re-derive family dimensions.

## 12. Naming Conventions

- Component IDs: `OHM-NNN` where NNN is the 3-digit backlog number (001-180). New additions (components not in the 180 backlog) start at `OHM-201` and increment.
- Slug: lowercase snake_case, e.g., `OHM-004 res_0603`. Display name stays the backlog name.
- Package family IDs: `PKG-<UPPER_SNAKE>` (e.g., `PKG-CHIP2T`, `PKG-SOIC`).
- Package member IDs: `<family>.<member>` (e.g., `PKG-CHIP2T.0603I` for imperial 0603).
- Generator IDs: `GEN-<UPPER_SNAKE>`.
- **Chip size naming**: imperial code is the default OHMNI name (0603 = 0603 imperial = 1608 metric). Every chip entry states both: `imperial: 0603, metric: 1608`. Metric codes are L x W in 0.1 mm. Known trap: "0603 metric" (0.6 x 0.3 mm) is the 0201 imperial; "01005 imperial" = "0402 metric" (0.4 x 0.2 mm); "0201 metric" = "008004 imperial". The backlog names mean imperial unless an entry says otherwise.
- Crystal codes (3225, 2520, 2016, 7050) are metric L x W in 0.1 mm.

## 13. Component ID Convention Summary

```
OHM-004            -> res_0603                (instance of PKG-CHIP2T.0603I, class B)
OHM-098            -> transistor_to220        (instance of PKG-TO220, class B or A)
PKG-CHIP2T         -> package family
GEN-CHIP_2T        -> generator
```

## 14. Required Entry Schema (summary)

Each entry uses these headings in order: Identity, Physical Dimensions, Geometry, Leads / Pins / Terminals, PCB Interface, Materials, Appearance, Orientation Markings, Recognition Features, Parametric Variants, Recommended Base Geometry, Modeling Procedure, LOD Strategy, Simplification Rules, Structured Specification (YAML), Sources, Research Confidence.

## 16. Research Rules (apply to every section)

1. Prefer S1 > S2 > S3 > S4 > S5. Do not cite random blogs, AI-written articles, image boards, or unsourced dimension tables when authoritative documents exist.
2. Cite only documents actually opened. Record URL, title, revision/date if shown.
3. Package != product. Where a package is standardized, establish nominal/common dimensions, accepted range, and meaningful manufacturer variation. Choose a clearly labeled OHMNI DEFAULT.
4. Never fabricate a JEDEC/IEC/EIA number. Never claim a package is standardized if it is only common practice (state "de facto").
5. Show conflicts between sources; do not hide them.
6. Mark gaps as `RESEARCH_REQUIRED` with exactly what is missing.
7. Validate: dimensions consistent, pitch x (N-1) fits the overall length, pin count matches geometry, pin-1 and polarity correct, metric/imperial naming not confused, no cross-manufacturer mixing.

---

## 17. Convention Addenda (added after wave-1 feedback; these are binding)

1. **Terminal position reference.** "Pin/terminal position" in YAML (`pin1_xy_mm`) means the center of the terminal's PCB-contact area (SMD underside center, or lead axis for THT), not the pad edge.
2. **4-pad SMD parts (common-mode chokes, 4-pad crystals/oscillators, 4-terminal LEDs):** viewed from top, pin 1 at the top-left (-X, +Y), counter-clockwise numbering (1 top-left, 2 bottom-left, 3 bottom-right, 4 top-right), unless the cited datasheet specifies otherwise (then follow the datasheet and record the delta).
3. **In-line 3-pin THT parts (resonators, TO-92 when viewed from top, 3-pin pots):** run along X with pin 1 at -X. Single-row multi-pin parts (SIP networks, headers, trimmers with 3 pins in a row) run along Y with pin 1 at +Y, per the single-row rule. The entry states which rule it uses and why.
4. **Arrays and long-side-terminal parts:** apply the dual-row rule (rows parallel to Y). This can rotate a part 90 degrees from the datasheet drawing; the entry must state the rotation applied.
5. **Additional material tokens (approved):** MAT_INDUCTOR_CERAMIC_TAN (#C9B48A, rough 0.7), MAT_RUBBER_SEAL (#1A1A1A, 0.8), MAT_CAP_DISC_COATING (#C8782A, 0.5), MAT_FILM_CASE_RED (#B3261E), MAT_FILM_CASE_YELLOW (#D9B92E), MAT_FILM_CASE_BLUE (#1F4E9E), MAT_MICA_DIP (#B5651D), MAT_COIL_LACQUER (#7A3B1E, 0.45), MAT_WIRE_ENAMEL_COPPER (#B8733A). Sections may propose more in their file; the coordinator merges.
6. **THT tail override.** The default tail bottom (-2.6 mm) is a default only; entries with long pins (for example snap-in electrolytics, 4 mm protrusion) override it explicitly in YAML via `terminals.tail_below_board_top_mm`.
7. **Research evidence level.** Most sources in this spec were read through a text-extraction fetch tool, not by visual inspection of drawings. Figures that depend on interpreting drawing callouts are capped at confidence M unless corroborated by a second document.

## 18. Resolved Conventions (decisions made after cross-checking all sections; binding for Codex)

1. **Dimension axis naming.** `overall_length` is the long body axis as drawn in the cited datasheet. For chip/axial/radial 2-terminal parts length runs along X (terminal to terminal). For dual-row parts (DIP, SOIC, TSSOP, SSOP, MSOP, DFN) length runs along Y (the direction of the pin rows) and `overall_width` runs along X (across the leads, lead tip to lead tip). Each entry's Geometry section restates the axis mapping; if an entry and this rule disagree, the entry's explicit coordinates win.
2. **PLCC pin 1.** PLCC-28 uses a `pin1_mode` parameter. Default `center_top` (pin 1 at the middle of the top side with numbering counter-clockwise), which is the J-lead convention recorded in G09; this overrides the quad rule in Section 6 for PLCC only. The convention was not confirmed in an opened primary document and is flagged in the entry.
3. **BGA/WLCSP orientation.** Ball grids are defined in TOP view (looking down at the package marking side after placement), A1 at the top-left corner, letters increase toward -Y, numbers increase toward +X. Manufacturer drawings are usually BOTTOM views (mirrored about the Y axis): mirror X when transcribing a bottom-view drawing. The row-letter skip rule (omitting I, O, Q, S, X, Z) is not confirmed in an opened source and stays a parameter.
4. **Display and module parts.** Viewing direction is +Z (viewed from above). Text reads along +X. Header rows of display modules may run along X; the entry states this and the mating direction. The single-row-along-Y rule applies only to discrete pin headers/terminals.
5. **Mating direction.** Side-entry/edge connectors mate toward +Y (the mating face may overhang the board edge). Top-entry parts (U.FL, vertical SMA, vertical USB-A, top-entry JST/KK headers) mate along +Z. Right-angle pin headers mate toward +X (G11 decision). FFC/FPC ZIF connectors have the contact row along X with cable insertion toward +Y (G12B decision, overriding the single-row-along-Y rule for this family).
6. **Vendor coordinate systems.** EDA libraries (KiCad: Y-down in the PCB editor) use different axes. Entries that took coordinates from such a source state the conversion applied (Y flipped to Y-up). Coordinates in YAML are always in the OHMNI frame of Section 2.
7. **Polarity convention.** For modeling, terminal 1 is the CATHODE for diodes and LEDs and the PLUS terminal for polarized capacitors, at -X, following the KiCad library convention. Other EDA libraries differ; importers must map by pad name, not by number alone.
8. **Pin 1 for 4-pad SMD parts.** Addendum 17.2 is the default; if the cited manufacturer datasheet defines pin 1 elsewhere (for example some crystals/oscillators put pin 1 at bottom-left), the entry follows the datasheet and records the delta. Codex must follow the entry.
9. **Tab holes and FCO.** Mounting/tab holes are included in the FCO bounding box only if they are footprint holes; the molded tab hole of a TO-220/TO-247 is part of the body and is NOT. For tabbed THT packages the lead plane sits at the body's thickness mid-plane unless the entry gives an offset.
10. **Status vocabulary.** `status: complete` = every key dimension is sourced (confidence M or better) or explicitly derived. `status: partial` = usable defaults exist but some values are UNCERTAIN/RECALLED_UNVERIFIED/RESEARCH_REQUIRED. `status: research_required` = the entry is a placeholder; do not implement dimensions from it without first resolving the listed gaps.
11. **Evidence level.** Section 17 item 7 applies to all entries. Several agents were additionally limited by a web-search budget and by fetch failures (documented per entry). Values tagged RECALLED_UNVERIFIED came from general engineering knowledge, not from an opened document, and must not be treated as sourced.
12. **Second-pass reconciliations.** After the gap-fill pass: SOT-23 contact |y| = 1.0 mm (3-lead) and 1.2 mm (5/6-lead) per PKG-SOT23 (G07), used by OHM-070, 094, 120, 121. SMD aluminum can (OHM-030) places the base-plate chamfer on the positive side (-X under the Section 18.7 polarity rule). SMD crystals/oscillators default to pin 1 at top-left (NDK/Epson), with Abracon's bottom-left kept as a variant. The 3.5 mm audio jack default is the Ledino KB3SPRS (KiCad-verified pins), larger than the PJ-307. Pluggable terminal OHM-161 defaults to the right-angle MSTBA header (plug mates +X). JST-SH side-entry OHM-157 mates toward -X so pin 1 at +Y is not mirrored.

# G01: Chip Passives (PKG-CHIP2T)

Group G01 covers OHM-001..009 (chip resistors), OHM-021..027 (MLCC), OHM-041..043 (chip inductors). All 19 entries instantiate the family PKG-CHIP2T (generator GEN-CHIP_2T). Family sections come first, entries after, proposed additions last.

Research note on sourcing: every document cited below was actually opened through WebFetch. Most were reached through distributor or third-party hosted copies (tier S4), not the manufacturer site, and the fetch tool returns a model-generated extraction of the PDF rather than raw text. Where an extraction looked internally inconsistent it is called out and the value was NOT used. No EIA, IEC or EIAJ size-code standard text was opened: size codes are therefore described as de facto industry naming that is cross-checked against the manufacturer tables below, never as a quoted standard.

---

## PACKAGE FAMILY: PKG-CHIP2T

### Shared geometry description

A chip two-terminal part is a rectangular block, length L along X, width W along Y, height T/H along Z, with two terminal bands at the X ends. The terminals are not separate leads. Each is a metallized end cap that wraps from the end face onto the top face, bottom face, and both side faces, so every terminal reads as a "five-face" metal cap (end face + four wrap faces) over a band length measured along X from the end face.

Wrap-around geometry by function:

- Thick-film chip resistor (Yageo, Vishay, KOA, Panasonic): the end face is fully metallized. The bottom band (the solder contact face, on the alumina substrate side) and the top band (on the overglaze side) have DIFFERENT lengths in the datasheets: Yageo gives I1 and I2, Vishay gives T1 and T2, KOA gives C and D, Panasonic gives a and b. The opened extractions do not state which letter is top and which is bottom, so the assignment of top vs bottom is RESEARCH_REQUIRED (drawing not seen). OHMNI treats the two lengths per size as "band_a" and "band_b" and assigns band_a to the top and band_b to the bottom as a labeled convention (see table). The visible effect is small (0.0 to 0.1 mm difference).
- MLCC: one termination band length B (KEMET symbol B, Murata symbol e, Samsung symbol BW) that wraps equally onto all four faces. The band is slightly proud of the ceramic. Ceramic is visible between the two caps on all four faces.
- Chip inductor: multilayer ferrite types have the same wrap-around cap as an MLCC (band length e). Wirewound ceramic types (Coilcraft CS) have a different, larger and non-nominal envelope (see variants).

1812 is in the family because OHM-027 (1812 MLCC) needs it. No 1812 chip resistor row was found in the opened resistor datasheets (Vishay, Yageo, KOA lists skip from 1210 to 1218/2010), so 1812 has `resistor_supported: false` in the table.

### Size-name table (imperial / metric)

The imperial code is the OHMNI name. The metric code is L x W in 0.1 mm of the nominal chip. Cross-check: the KEMET table (opened) pairs 0201/0603, 0402/1005, 0603/1608, 0805/2012, 1206/3216, 1210/3225, 1812/4532 (EIA/metric). Vishay pairs 2010/5025 and 2512/6332. Murata's size-code list (opened) shows code 01 = 0.25 x 0.125 mm as EIA 008004 and code 03 = 0.6 x 0.3 mm as EIA 0201, confirming the Section 12 trap. The 01005 imperial = 0402 metric (0.4 x 0.2 mm) pairing comes from the Yageo RC0100 (0.40 x 0.20) and KOA 1F "01005" (0.4 x 0.2) rows; the "0402 metric" name itself was not opened in any document (naming inference, no source text).

### Generator notes (GEN-CHIP_2T)

Inputs: L, W, T (height), band_len_a (top), band_len_b (bottom), band_len_end default = max(a,b), function in {R, C, L}, color tokens, marking decal, polarity none.

Procedure (shared): build body box centered at XY origin with bottom at Z = 0; build two end caps; cut/inset the top face between caps for the resistor coat; apply materials per function.

Notes:
- Terminals lie on the X axis, terminal 1 at -X (architecture Section 6). Pad-pattern centroid equals body centroid, so `body_offset_mm = [0, 0]`.
- End caps: OHMNI modeling default cap proud-ness 0.02 mm for sizes <= 0402, 0.03 mm for larger (UNCERTAIN, visual convention only, not sourced).
- Resistor top coat inset: coat spans X between the top band inner edges; coat thickness OHMNI modeling default 0.03 mm (UNCERTAIN, visual only).
- Edge radii: LOD2 only, 0.02 to 0.05 mm (UNCERTAIN, not sourced).
- Solder fillets and pads are excluded (architecture Section 5).
- Land patterns (IPC-7351) were not researched here; the footprint layer owns pads.

### Appearance common to the family

Resistor (visual defaults; the opened datasheets do not state colors): black or dark overglaze top (MAT_RESISTOR_COAT_BLACK), white to off-white alumina visible on the sides and underside (MAT_CERAMIC_ALUMINA_WHITE), tin-plated terminals (MAT_TIN_MATTE). The Yageo datasheet says "epoxy coat" protective finish and "high-grade ceramic body". The colors are widely seen practice but are NOT confirmed by an opened document: confidence L for color. Marking: Yageo states RC0075, RC0100, RC0201 and RC0402 are unmarked; RC0603 uses a 3-digit (E24) or EIA-96 code; RC0805 and larger use 3-digit (5%) or 4-digit (1% and tighter). Panasonic notes some series lack top-side value marking. Marking is white text, decal only.

MLCC (visual defaults): unmarked (KEMET states supplied unmarked for C0G; laser marking not available on C0G; the C1812C224J sheet says Marked: No). Body color varies by dielectric: X7R/X5R tan to brown (MAT_MLCC_BROWN), C0G/NP0 gray-ish tan (MAT_MLCC_GRAY). The color mapping is OHMNI default, not from an opened datasheet. Terminals: Cu or Ag inner electrode, Ni barrier, matte Sn outer (Samsung: inner electrode Ni, termination Cu, plating Ni/Sn 100%; KEMET: copper external electrode, nickel barrier, matte tin).

Chip inductor (visual defaults): multilayer ferrite = dark gray to black-brown body (MAT_FERRITE_DARK), tin terminals. Wirewound ceramic (Coilcraft 0805CS: "marked with a single dot", color varies by value) = ceramic body with dot. Other manufacturers' body colors were not opened: confidence L.

### Terminal plating layers

Resistor: Yageo "matte tin on Ni-barrier"; Vishay "pure tin solder contacts on Ni barrier layer"; KOA lists inner electrode, Ni plating, Sn plating; Panasonic lists inner, middle, outer electrodes (three layers). MLCC: as above. Layer thickness not sourced (not modeled, finish only).

### Family confidence

Dimensions: M for L/W (resistor, MLCC) and H/T of resistors and MLCC T/B for 1206/1210 (gap-fill pass); L for inductor 1206 e only. Geometry: H (wrap-around, five-face cap shape widely consistent with the band-length symbols in every datasheet). Materials/appearance: L-M (colors not documented in opened sources).

Validation: L x W checked against metric code names for all ten members (for example 3225 -> 3.2 x 2.5, 4532 -> 4.5 x 3.2). Cross-manufacturer mixing: resistor H and bands from Yageo only, MLCC T/B from Murata/KEMET/Samsung with source named per cell. Panasonic table rejected for row shift. Band length is always less than L/2 (largest ratio 0.60 / 6.3).

# [OHM-001] 01005 SMD resistor
## Identity
- Canonical name: 01005 SMD resistor (thick-film chip resistor)
- ID: OHM-001; slug: res_01005
- Category: passive; Subcategory: resistor, chip, thick film
- Physical package: PKG-CHIP2T.01005I (imperial 01005, metric 0402); generator GEN-CHIP_2T
- Mounting type: smd
- Aliases: R01005, chip resistor 01005, 0402 metric, RC01005 (Yageo series prefix), CRCW01005 (Vishay series prefix)
- Common variants: 0 ohm jumper (same body), precision thin film (RG-style, same outline), current sense (OHM-014, wide-terminal variant, owned by G02)
- Class B; priority P3; complexity 3

## Physical Dimensions
Family member row (see PKG-CHIP2T resistor table), values restated:
- overall_length L: default 0.4, min 0.38, max 0.42; basis MFR_DATASHEET; confidence M
- overall_width W: default 0.2, min 0.18, max 0.22; basis same; confidence M
- overall_height H: default 0.13, min 0.11, max 0.15; basis MFR_DATASHEET (Yageo RC_L; Vishay differs, see below); confidence M
- terminal band lengths: band_a (top) 0.1, band_b (bottom) 0.1; basis MFR_DATASHEET (Yageo I1/I2); confidence M; top/bottom assignment is RESEARCH_REQUIRED (drawing not seen)
- Conflicts: None between R1 and R3 on L/W/H; R3 band D 0.11 vs R1 0.10.

## Geometry
- Primary shape: rectangular alumina substrate block 0.4 x 0.2 x 0.13 mm, bottom at Z = 0.
- Secondary: black overglaze coat on the top face spanning the gap between the two top bands (coat thickness modeling default 0.03 mm, UNCERTAIN, visual only).
- Terminals: two wrap-around end caps, each covering the full end face, with a top band of 0.1 mm and a bottom band of 0.1 mm measured from the end face, and a side wrap of the same length on both side faces (side wrap length is not sourced; OHMNI default = min(top, bottom) band, UNCERTAIN).
- Sides of the substrate between caps show white alumina on the Y faces. No chamfers at LOD1. Edge radius LOD2 only.

## Leads / Pins / Terminals
- Count 2; type: wrap-around metallized end cap (flat_pad on the underside).
- Terminal 1 at -X, terminal 2 at +X. Terminal envelope along X: end face to 0.1 mm inboard on the bottom.

- Aliases: R1210, chip resistor 1210, 3225 metric, RC1210 (Yageo series prefix), CRCW1210 (Vishay series prefix)
- Common variants: 0 ohm jumper (same body), precision thin film (RG-style, same outline), current sense (OHM-014, wide-terminal variant, owned by G02)
- Class B; priority P1; complexity 2

## Physical Dimensions
Family member row (see PKG-CHIP2T resistor table), values restated:
- overall_length L: default 3.2, min 3.00, max 3.4; basis CONSENSUS; confidence M
- overall_width W: default 2.5, min 2.3, max 2.75; basis same; confidence M
- overall_height H: default 0.55, min 0.45, max 0.65; basis MFR_DATASHEET (Yageo RC_L; Vishay differs, see below); confidence M
- terminal band lengths: band_a (top) 0.45, band_b (bottom) 0.45; basis MFR_DATASHEET (Yageo I1/I2); confidence M; top/bottom assignment is RESEARCH_REQUIRED (drawing not seen)
- Conflicts: L: R1 3.10 vs R2/R3 3.2; W: R1 2.60 vs R2/R3 2.5. Default 3.20 x 2.50 per metric name 3225.

## Geometry
- Primary shape: rectangular alumina substrate block 3.2 x 2.5 x 0.55 mm, bottom at Z = 0.
- Secondary: black overglaze coat on the top face spanning the gap between the two top bands (coat thickness modeling default 0.03 mm, UNCERTAIN, visual only).
- Terminals: two wrap-around end caps, each covering the full end face, with a top band of 0.45 mm and a bottom band of 0.45 mm measured from the end face, and a side wrap of the same length on both side faces (side wrap length is not sourced; OHMNI default = min(top, bottom) band, UNCERTAIN).
- Sides of the substrate between caps show white alumina on the Y faces. No chamfers at LOD1. Edge radius LOD2 only.

## Leads / Pins / Terminals
- Count 2; type: wrap-around metallized end cap (flat_pad on the underside).
- Terminal 1 at -X, terminal 2 at +X. Terminal envelope along X: end face to 0.45 mm inboard on the bottom.
- Terminal center X on the underside: +/-1.375 mm. Terminal width = W (2.5), full width.
- Material MAT_TIN_MATTE over (invisible) Ni barrier; fully modeled as one visible shell.
- Numbering: terminal 1 at -X; no electrical polarity.

## PCB Interface
- Footprint type smd_pads; standoff 0; thermal pad none.
- FCO origin (pad pattern centroid) coincides with the body center, so body_offset_mm = [0, 0].
- Pin 1 (terminal 1 center on underside) at (-1.375, 0). Terminal 2 at (1.375, 0).
- Body underside at Z = 0. Land pattern is not part of this entry (IPC-7351 land patterns not researched).

## Materials
- Terminals: MAT_TIN_MATTE
- Top coat: MAT_RESISTOR_COAT_BLACK
- Substrate (sides, underside between bands): MAT_CERAMIC_ALUMINA_WHITE
- Marking decal (where applicable): MAT_SILKSCREEN_WHITE (decal only). No new tokens.

## Appearance
- Geometry vs decal separated. Top: black glossy (OHMNI default; the datasheets only say epoxy/glass protective coat, so color is unconfirmed, confidence L). Sides and underside: white alumina. Terminals: matte tin.
- Marking: 3-digit (5%) or 4-digit (1%) code. Marking is a white 3 or 4 character decal on the top face centered between the bands; omit when unmarked.
- Manufacturer variation: top coat can be dark gray, blue-gray or black; some series have no marking (Panasonic remark, R4).

## Orientation Markings
- None required (non-polarized). Terminal 1 at -X by convention only; mirror-symmetric part.
- Value marking text reads along X when viewed from the top at rotation 0.

## Recognition Features
1. Aspect ratio L:W = 1.28:1 rectangle with two silver-gray end caps.
2. Black top face with white alumina visible on the long side faces.
3. End caps wrap onto top and bottom with a visible band of 0.45 mm (top).
4. Height 0.55 mm, much thinner than the width; flat low profile.
5. Value marking present.

## Parametric Variants
- Safe parameters: L, W, H, band_a, band_b, coat_thickness, cap_proudness, marking_text.
- Coupled: band_a + band_b < L (always, max ratio 1.1/L); H >= coat_thickness + 0.05; W stays at family value (do not swap W and L); keeping imperial name fixed.
- Function swap (R to C to L) changes only materials and marking, not the outline.

## Recommended Base Geometry
One box (substrate) 3.2 x 2.5 x 0.55; one thin box (coat) on top; two end-cap shells made by boolean union of an end-face slab, a top slab, a bottom slab and two side slabs; decal plane on the coat.

## Modeling Procedure
1. Create substrate box centered at X,Y = 0, Z from 0 to 0.55.
2. Create two end caps at X = +/-L/2 covering full W and H, band lengths per face above.
3. Insert the black coat box between top band inner edges at Z from 0.52 to 0.55 (flush with cap top).
4. Assign materials; apply marking decal if marked.
5. Verify bottom of caps at Z = 0 and that no part crosses Z < 0.

## LOD Strategy
- LOD0: single box 3.2 x 2.5 x 0.55 plus two end boxes (no coat inset, no decal).
- LOD1: substrate + coat inset + two wrap-around caps (end, top, bottom, sides), marking decal.
- LOD2: LOD1 plus edge radii 0.02 to 0.05 mm and slight cap proud-ness.

## Simplification Rules
- May omit: marking, edge radii, cap proud-ness, coat inset below 0.02 mm height (for 01005 and 0201 treat coat as a color change only).
- Never omit: both end caps, the black-top / white-side color split, correct L x W x H, terminal 1 at -X.

# G02: Non-chip resistors, networks, potentiometers (OHM-010 to OHM-020)

Status of this file: written by research agent G02. Convention source: 00_architecture.md (FCO origin, Z up, top view +X right / +Y up, MAT_* tokens, confidence system). Dimensions are mm unless suffixed.

**How to read the confidence flags.** Most manufacturer PDFs were read through a fetch tool that summarizes the page text. Tabular dimension tables (Yageo, Vishay text tables) came through cleanly. Drawing callouts (Bourns trimmers and pots, Alpha pots, Vishay WSBS shunt) came through as loose numbers with ambiguous label association. Where a number's association to a feature was inferred, the row says so and the confidence is capped at M or L. Nothing was filled from memory without being labeled UNCERTAIN.

**Standardization statement (applies to all axial parts).** No IEC or JEDEC body-size table for axial resistors was opened. IEC 60063 (preferred number series) and IEC 60062 (marking codes) were NOT confirmed as body-size standards. IEC 60294 (dimension measurement of axial-lead cylindrical components) exists, but its VDE preview could not be fetched (robots.txt failure), so its content is unverified here. One reference page (eepower.com, S5) states "The size of axial resistors is not as standardized as the SMD resistors, and different manufacturers often use slightly different dimensions." Therefore everything below is DE FACTO (manufacturer-published sizes that happen to be close to each other). Vishay MBA/B/E datasheet states that four or five color rings designate value and tolerance "in accordance with IEC 60062" (so band MARKING is standardized; body SIZE is not). Names like "0204 / 0207 / 0414" are Vishay's own type designators (de facto in industry, close to DIN-style names), not verified IEC sizes.

**Tokens proposed (not in 00_architecture.md Section 7), used by this group:**

| Token | Use | Base color | Roughness | Metallic |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MAT_RESISTOR_PAINT_BEIGE | carbon-film body lacquer | #D8C7A3 | 0.6 | 0 |
| MAT_RESISTOR_PAINT_BLUE | metal-film body lacquer (de facto light blue) | #6FA3C7 | 0.55 | 0 |
| MAT_RESISTOR_PAINT_GREEN | silicone/enamel wirewound coating (color not source-verified) | #4F7A4A | 0.6 | 0 |
| MAT_PLASTIC_BLUE | cermet trimmer housing (de facto) | #1E5AA8 | 0.45 | 0 |
| MAT_BRASS | adjust screw, potentiometer wiper hardware | #C9A24A | 0.35 | 1.0 |
| MAT_ALLOY_MANGANIN | shunt resistive element | #8A6F55 | 0.4 | 1.0 |
| MAT_BAND_* | decal-only colors for color bands (black #111, brown #6B3A1E, red #C0281E, orange #E8751A, yellow #E8C81A, green #2E8B3E, blue #2756B8, violet #7A3FA0, gray #8C8C8C, white #F2F2F0, gold #C9A23A, silver #BFC1C4) | | | |

## PACKAGE FAMILY: PKG-AXIAL_RES

**Scope.** Axial-lead cylindrical film resistors (carbon film OHM-010, metal film OHM-011). Generator: GEN-AXIAL. Standardization: DE FACTO (see header). Power ratings 1/8 W to 2 W.

**Shared geometry.**
- Body: cylinder along X, diameter D, length L, axis at Z = D/2 + standoff (standoff 0), body centered at X=0, Y=0. Both ends: thin end caps or shallow shoulders (LOD2 only, de facto, no dimensions sourced; default cap = same diameter, 0.1 mm radius round-over).
- Leads: wire diameter d, axis on the body axis (Y=0, Z=D/2). Each lead leaves the body end horizontally, runs to X = +/-P/2, bends 90 deg downward with inner bend radius default 1.0*d (de facto), runs straight down and ends at Z = -(board_thickness + 1.0) = -2.6 (LOD1). Datasheet "H" lead length (26 to 35 mm) is the uncut length on a taped part and is NOT modeled; the formed/cut lead is.
- Lead pitch P (hole spacing) is a footprint choice. NO opened datasheet specifies it. OHMNI rule (DERIVED, UNCERTAIN): P = smallest multiple of 2.54 mm that is >= L_nom + 4*d. Hard minimum P >= L_max + 2*(d + bend_radius).
- Color bands: decals on the cylinder, bands wrap 360 deg. Layout in fractions of body length L measured from terminal 1 (-X) end (OHMNI default decal positions, DERIVED, not from a datasheet):
  - 4-band (value 2 digits, multiplier, tolerance): b1 [0.12, 0.20], b2 [0.26, 0.34], b3 [0.40, 0.48], tolerance [0.80, 0.88].
  - 5-band (value 3 digits, multiplier, tolerance): b1 [0.10, 0.17], b2 [0.22, 0.29], b3 [0.34, 0.41], b4 [0.46, 0.53], tolerance [0.83, 0.90].
  - Reading direction: first band is the one nearest terminal 1 (-X). Tolerance band is separated by a visibly larger gap. Band color decode tables are not repeated (Section 8 of architecture).

**Member dimension table.** All rows: Yageo CFR datasheet v2 (Sep 27 2023) for carbon film and Yageo MFR datasheet (no revision shown) for metal film, which list identical dimensions for CFR-xx and MFR-xx. Cross-checks: Vishay MBA/MBB/MBE (professional metal film, rev 11-Jul-2018, maximum values) and eepower.com table (S5). Basis for default: MFR_DATASHEET (Yageo) with cross-check; "CONSENSUS" is NOT claimed because Yageo CFR and MFR are one manufacturer and the Vishay values are maxima for different power ratings.

| Member | Yageo type | Rated P (Yageo) | L nominal +/- | D nominal +/- | lead d +/- | H lead (uncut) | Vishay cross-check | eepower cross-check | OHMNI default P (pitch rule) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AX_1_6W (called 1/8 W in many catalogs) | CFR-12 / MFR-12 | 1/6 W | 3.4 +/-0.3 | 1.9 +/-0.2 | 0.45 +/-0.05 | 28 +/-2 | MBA/SMA 0204: Lmax 3.6, Dmax 1.6, d 0.5, 0.4 W (different rating class) | "1/8 W": 3.0+/-0.3 x 1.8+/-0.3, d 0.45 | 7.62 |
| AX_1_4W | CFR-25 / MFR-25 | 1/4 W | 6.3 +/-0.5 | 2.4 +/-0.2 | 0.55 +/-0.05 | 28 +/-2 | MBB/SMA 0207: Lmax 6.5, Dmax 2.5, d 0.6, 0.6 W | 6.5+/-0.5 x 2.5+/-0.3, d 0.6 | 10.16 |
| AX_1_2W | CFR-50 / MFR-50 | 1/2 W | 9.0 +/-0.5 | 3.3 +/-0.3 | 0.55 +/-0.05 | 26 +/-2 | none | 8.5+/-0.5 x 3.2+/-0.3, d 0.6 | 12.70 |
| AX_1W | CFR-100 / MFR100 | 1 W | 11.5 +/-1.0 | 4.5 +/-0.5 | 0.8 +/-0.05 | 35 +/-2 | MBE/SMA 0414: Lmax 11.9, Dmax 4.2, d 0.8, 1.0 W | 11+/-1 x 5+/-0.5, d 0.8 | 15.24 |
| AX_2W | CFR-200 / MFR200 | 2 W | 15.5 +/-1.0 | 5.0 +/-0.5 | 0.8 +/-0.05 | 33 +/-2 | none | none | 20.32 |

Notes: Yageo lists 1/6 W (not 1/8 W) for the smallest style; the backlog's "1/8 W" body maps to this row, with eepower's 3.0 x 1.8 as the conflicting smaller value. MFR25S/50S/1WS/2WS/3WS miniature variants have "identical dimensional parameters" per the Yageo MFR sheet (this was the summary tool's statement; treat as M). Vishay MBA/B/E values are MAXIMA (Dmax, Lmax). Conflict: Vishay 0207 max 6.5 x 2.5 vs Yageo 6.3+/-0.5 x 2.4+/-0.2, consistent within tolerance. Vishay mass: 125 / 220 / 700 mg for 0204 / 0207 / 0414 (irrelevant to modeling).

OHMNI defaults: use the Yageo nominal values in the table. min = nominal - tol, max = nominal + tol.

**Generator parameters.** rated_power (selects row), L, D, d, pitch P, band_count (4|5), body_color_token, band decals list, lead_tail_bottom (-2.6). Coupled: P >= L + 4d; D < L; lead axis Z = D/2.

**Sources (family).**

2. Yageo, "Metal Film Resistors General Type Normal & Miniature Style [MFR Series]", no revision shown, S3/S4. URL opened: https://www.pdp8online.com/mfm/board/datasheets/Yageo_MFR.pdf. Gave MFR dimension table (identical to CFR).
3. Vishay, "MBA/SMA 0204, MBB/SMA 0207, MBE/SMA 0414 Professional Metal Film Leaded Resistors", revision 11-Jul-2018, S3. URL opened: http://www.vishay.com/docs/28766/mbxsma.pdf. Gave max body sizes, d, mass, IEC 60062 four/five-ring statement.
4. eepower.com "Resistor Sizes and Packages", S5. URL opened: https://eepower.com/resistor-guide/resistor-standards-and-codes/resistor-sizes-and-packages/. Gave a generic size table and the "not as standardized" statement. Cross-check only.

## PACKAGE FAMILY: PKG-POWER_RES

**Scope.** Axial power resistors: cement-case rectangular block (OHM-012) and wirewound ceramic-tube (OHM-013). Generator: GEN-AXIAL (power variant). De facto, no standard confirmed.

**Cement style (Yageo SQP/NSP).** Body is a rectangular-section ceramic/cement case (W x H separately toleranced in the datasheet; for 2 W both are 7.0). Leads exit the center of the two end faces, axis at Z = H/2. The Yageo summary text also said "cylindrical bodies oriented horizontally", which conflicts with independent W and H columns; the independent W and H are treated as the stronger evidence (M). Marking example from the datasheet: "YAGEO 1801 10WN 100R J" (brand, date code, power, N = non-inductive suffix, value, tolerance) printed on the side face.

| CEM_3W | SQP300 / NSP300 | 22 +/-1.5 | 8.0 +/-1.0 | 8.0 +/-1.0 | 0.8 +/-0.05 | 25.40 |
| CEM_5W | SQP500 / NSP500 | 22 +/-1.5 | 9.5 +/-1.0 | 9.0 +/-1.0 | 0.8 +/-0.05 | 25.40 |

Lead length: only the SQP40A variant states L1 = 28 +/-3.0 (not in the table above); other lead lengths are not given. The pitch column is DERIVED by OHMNI and not a manufacturer value; real footprints vary with how the user bends the leads (UNCERTAIN). Opened SQP500 spec page (yageogroup.com) repeated L 22 +/-1.5, W 9.5 +/-1.0, H 9.0 +/-1.0, d 0.8 +/-0.05, confirming the table.

**Wirewound ceramic-tube style (Vishay Dale RS/NS, axial).** Datasheet "Wirewound Resistors, Industrial, Precision Power, Silicone Coated, Axial Lead", Vishay doc 30204. Dimension table in inches (conversion to mm by OHMNI). Column reading: the datasheet header letters are A, B(max), C, D. Gap-fill pass: two further fetches (vishay.com/docs/30204/rsns.pdf and farnell.com/datasheets/2049176.pdf) read the drawing labels as A = body length, B (max.) = overall length, C = body diameter, D = lead diameter, with the table note "(3) B (max.) dimension is clean lead to clean lead" (the second read also called D 'wire diameter', which conflicts with the plausibility check; D = lead diameter adopted because D = 1.02 for the 5 W part is a lead size, not a resistance wire). B cannot be the full lead-to-lead length (leads are 38.10 min each), so it is read as the span of the body including the metal end caps and the bare ('clean') lead stubs, i.e. B >= A. OHMNI adopts: end-cap protrusion per side = (B - A)/2 (DERIVED interpretation, L-M; RS005: (25.40 - 22.23)/2 = 1.59). Coating color is still not stated in either read.

## PACKAGE FAMILY: PKG-SHUNT

**Scope.** Metal strip shunt resistors, high current, low value. Two physical styles, both de facto and manufacturer-specific. Generator: GEN-SIP (backlog naming), recommended implementation as GEN-SHUNT (strip + terminal blocks + optional sense pins). STATUS: PARTIAL.

**Style A: SMD precision strip "3920" (Isabellenhutte BVS).** Opened datasheet "ISA-WELD Precision Resistor" (BVS, Issue 24-January-2025). Dimensions (BVS-xxx 3920 case): L 10 +0.3, W 5.2 +0.3/-0.2, H 0.5 +/-0.1 (the datasheet's "H"; most likely the resistive-element thickness, overall height with terminal plating/welds RESEARCH_REQUIRED). Land pattern letters: l = 11 mm, w = 6.2 mm, a = 2.7 mm, x = 5.6 mm (BVS-Z-R0001: a = 3.6, x = 3.8); interpretation of a and x not established (likely pad length and pad gap), RESEARCH_REQUIRED. The rhopoint page notes "heavy copper connections ideally suited for mounting on DBC substrate" and 3920 size 5.2 x 10 mm. Imperial "3920" = 0.39 x 0.20 in = 9.9 x 5.1 mm (consistent).

**Style B: bolt-on metal strip with welded copper terminals and sense pins (Vishay WSBS8518...35).** Opened: length 60 +/-0.30 mm, thickness 3.00 +/-0.05 mm, terminal bolt hole diameter 7 +/-0.10 mm, sense pin spacing 9 mm ref., element = "solid metal nickel-chrome alloy", "welded terminal to element construction". Width and height columns are labeled A and B and vary with resistance (A: 3.05 / 15.62 / 22.86 mm for 100 / 500 / 1000 micro-ohm; B: 3.43 / 17.65 / 24.89 mm). Their meaning (width of strip vs. dimension of terminal pad/hole location) could NOT be established. RESEARCH_REQUIRED: strip width, hole center distance, hole center to end distance, sense pin protrusion, overall height. Ohmite SH series (metal-clad, 100 to 300 A) ordering sheet was opened but its values came back inconsistent (e.g., a 400 mm width, 60 mm height), so it is NOT used.

**Gap-fill correction (Style B).** Re-opened vishay.com/docs/30355/wsbs8518-35.pdf (one read gave the first-pass "length 60", a second, targeted read quoted "3.346 +/-0.016 (85 +/-0.41)" as OVERALL LENGTH, "0.708 +/-0.008 (18 +/-0.20)" as OVERALL WIDTH, thickness 0.118 +/-0.002 (3.00 +/-0.05), hole dia 7 +/-0.10, sense pin spacing 0.354 +/-0.010 (9 +/-0.25), chamfer 1.98 x 45 deg typ.) and the sibling sheet vishay.com/docs/30134/wsbs8518.pdf (read: 85 +/-0.4 length, 18 width, hole diameter 7, "hole spacing 2.362 in = 60 mm center-to-center", resistance-dependent A and B columns). The part name WSBS8518 (85 x 18 mm) also supports 85. CONCLUSION: the first-pass "60" is the HOLE CENTER SPACING (60 = 2.362 in), not the overall length; the 15.62 "width" is not a width: A (3.05 / 15.62 / 22.86 for 100 / 500 / 1000 micro-ohm; "A reference") and B (3.43 / 17.65 / 24.89, +/-0.13) are lengths of the resistive element along X (B = A + 0.38 or +2.03 or +2.03, B probably the element including welds). The sibling sheet's A/B for 50 to 250 micro-ohm (A 3.68 to 22.86) have the same role. Adopted OHMNI default for the "...35" part: overall length 85, width 18, thickness 3.0, holes dia 7 at X = +/-30 (c-c 60, from the sibling sheet only, M-L), element length A = 15.62 (500 micro-ohm default, B 17.65), terminal blocks each (85 - B)/2 = 33.7 long. The sibling sheet also showed a height 12.5 for WSBS8518...-xx in its summary read (a different, thicker variant or a mis-read); not used.
Sense-pin placement: the 9 +/-0.25 spacing is confirmed as a dimension but its axis (along the strip or across the width) and offset were not determinable from text (note: with A up to 22.86 a +/-4.5 pair along X would sit inside the element for most values, so the pins likely sit on the terminal blocks next to the element; unresolved). OHMNI default: two pins on the centerline at X = +/-4.5 (L) as the visual placeholder.

**OHMNI default for OHM-015** (representative, revised): Style B: strip 85 x 18 x 3.0 mm, hole dia 7 at X = +/-30, element length 15.62, sense pins 2x at 9 mm spacing, pin dia 1.0 (UNCERTAIN). status: partial (sense-pin geometry and the 85-vs-60 reading rest on two fetches of the same sheet).

**Sources (family).**

## PACKAGE FAMILY: PKG-SIP_NET

**Scope.** Single-in-line conformal-coated or molded thick-film resistor networks on 2.54 mm (0.100 in) pitch. Bussed (common pin 1) or isolated. Generator: GEN-SIP. De facto family (Bourns 4600X, Vishay MSP/CSC are drop-in compatible by catalog, not by standard).

**Body.** Rectangular block, narrow in thickness. Row of N leads along Y at pitch 2.54. Body length (along the row) = 2.54*N - 0.05 maximum (Bourns 4600X formula text; the datasheet text says "less .005 mm (.002 in)" but the table values prove it is 0.05 mm: N=6 gives 15.19, N=8 gives 20.27, N=10 gives 25.35, N=14 gives 35.51). Height (above PCB, along Z): Bourns 5.08 max labeled "body width" in the read; cross-check with Vishay MSP "A profile" height 4.95 (0.195 in) supports this being the height. "C profile" (MSP) height 8.89 (0.350 in). Body thickness (across the row): Bourns "3.3 +0.5/-0.3". The label assignment (height vs. thickness) of the two Bourns numbers is DERIVED from the Vishay cross-check, M confidence.

**Leads.** Pitch 2.54 +/-0.07 non-accumulating (Bourns). Lead cross-section: Bourns reads "0.254 +/-0.050 max" (diameter/thickness); Vishay MSP lead diameter 0.305 +/-0.076 (0.012 in) with exposed length 2.29 max (0.090 in). Bourns also lists ".508 +/-.050 typical both ends" whose meaning is unclear (possibly lead width or stub), not used. Conflict shown, OHMNI default: lead as a flat/round wire of 0.30 x 0.30 (UNCERTAIN, between sources), exposed length below body 2.29 (Vishay max; bodies sit at standoff 0 for modeling), so tail bottom Z = -2.29 (differs from the architecture default -2.6; entry notes this).

**Schematics (marking only).** Bussed ("101" Bourns, "01" Vishay): resistors from common pin 1 to each other pin; N-1 resistors for N pins (Bourns: 3 to 13 resistors; Vishay: 5 to 9 resistors with common pin). Isolated ("102" Bourns, "03" Vishay): N/2 resistors, each between two pins (Bourns: 2 to 7). Vishay also lists schematic "05" dual terminator.

**Pin-1 marking.** Both datasheets show a pin #1 identification on the drawing; form (dot, notch, printed) is not described in the text read. OHMNI default: printed dot at the pin-1 end of the face (LOD1 decal) plus the bussed variant shows pin 1 as the common pin. RESEARCH_REQUIRED for the exact mark style.

**Member table (Bourns 4600X).**

| Member | Pins N | Body length max |
|---|---|---|
| SIP_6 | 6 | 15.19 |
| SIP_8 | 8 | 20.27 |
| SIP_10 | 10 | 25.35 |
| SIP_14 | 14 | 35.51 |
| SIP_N (generic) | N | 2.54*N - 0.05 |

Vishay MSP lists MSP06 14.99, MSP08 20.07, MSP09 22.61, MSP10 25.15 (these are 2.54*N - 0.25; smaller than Bourns by 0.2 mm; conflict shown, family default follows Bourns).

**Orientation convention note.** The architecture's single-row rule is written for headers. Applied here by analogy: row along Y, pin 1 at +Y end, numbering toward -Y, body thickness along X. Flagged as a convention gap in the final report.

**Sources (family).**
1. Bourns, "4600X Series - Thick Film Conformal SIPs", REV. 04/10, S3/S4. URL opened: https://www.mouser.com/datasheet/2/54/bourns_4600x-1159064.pdf.
2. Vishay Dale, "MSP Thick Film Resistor Networks, Single-In-Line, Molded SIP", doc 31510, revision 13-Feb-15, S3. URL opened: https://www.vishay.com/docs/31510/msp.pdf.

## PACKAGE FAMILY: PKG-CHIP_ARRAY

**Scope.** Surface-mount resistor arrays: 2 or 4 or 8 resistors in one ceramic chip, terminations on the two long sides. Convex (terminals bulge slightly past the body edge, Yageo "YC") and concave (terminals are notches/half-moons in the edge, Yageo "TC"). Generator: GEN-CHIP_ARRAY. De facto, manufacturer drawings only (EIA/JEDEC outlines not opened).

**Evidence used.** Yageo "Array Chip Resistors YC/TC 5 %, 1 % sizes", Product specification September 25 2025 V.11 (S3). The read provided Table 1 columns H/H1/HW, B, P, L, T, W1, W2 but not their definitions, so the column roles are INFERRED by OHMNI from consistency checks (below). The datasheet says the body is ceramic with internal electrodes, protective epoxy overcoat, termination matte tin on Ni barrier; YC102/YC104 are "flat type"; the TC series is concave. YC162 was removed in version 10. Terminal counts and pin numbering were not in the read text.

**Column inference (DERIVED, M-L).** L = body length along the terminal row; W2 = body width across; T = body height; P = terminal pitch along L; W1 = terminal width along L; H = terminal length across the width (check: 2*H + center gap = W2). Check examples: YC164: 2*0.65 + gap 0.30 = 1.60 OK (W2 1.60); YC124: 2*0.40 + 0.20 = 1.00 OK; YC324: 2*1.10 + 1.0 = 3.2 OK. B is probably a terminal/rim feature (0.2 to 0.5), unresolved. The terminal count per side is DERIVED from L, P, W1: n_per_side = floor((L - W1)/P) + 1 (YC164: (3.2-0.3)/0.8 = 3.6 -> 4; YC122: (1.0-0.25)/0.67 = 1.1 -> 2; YC124: (2.0-0.30)/0.5 = 3.4 -> 4; YC248: (4.0-0.4)/0.5 = 7.2 -> 8; YC324: (5.08-0.5)/1.27 = 3.6 -> 4).

Agreement: L 3.20, W 1.60, P 0.80, T 0.50 to 0.60, terminal width 0.30, terminal length across 0.65 (Panasonic A1 = Yageo H = 0.65; A2 0.45 vs H1 0.50 = the shorter top-face wrap; G 0.35 = center gap, and 2*0.65 + 0.35 = 1.65 matches W within tolerance). This confirms the first-pass column inference: H = terminal length across (A1), H1 = top-side wrap length (A2), W1 or B = terminal width. EXB-28V (0402x4): L 2.00, W 1.00, T 0.35, A1 0.45, A2 0.35, B 0.20, P 0.50, G 0.25 (agrees with Yageo YC124 within tolerance: T 0.45 vs 0.35 and terminal width 0.30 vs 0.20 differ). EXB-2HV (0402x8, 16 terminals): L 3.80, W 1.60, T 0.45, A1 0.35, B 0.30, P 0.50, G 0.30 (Yageo YC248: L 4.00, W 1.60: 0.2 mm conflict, Yageo adopted as the family row). Pin 1: none of Yageo YC/TC (no pin or orientation text; YC102, YC122, TC122 and TC124 are listed as "No marking"), Vishay CRA06P or the Panasonic catalog page described a pin-1 mark; arrays are not marked in many sizes, so pin 1 is a CAD convention: OHMNI default remains an optional decal dot.

**Geometry.** Rectangular alumina body (bottom), black overglaze top (MAT_RESISTOR_COAT_BLACK), epoxy edge (not separately modeled). Convex: each termination is a box wrapping the long edge, top and bottom wrap, with small bulge outward (T of terminal plating ~0.02 outside the body, de facto, LOD2). Concave: each termination sits in a half-circle/rectangular notch cut into the long edge; the metallization lines the notch and wraps top/bottom. Terminals are identical in pitch, one row on each long side, number equal on both sides.

**OHMNI orientation per architecture dual-row rule:** rows parallel to Y (terminals on the -X and +X sides), pin 1 at top-left (-X, +Y), counting down the -X side then up the +X side. Note: datasheets draw arrays with terminals on long sides top and bottom in landscape view; the architecture rule rotates this by 90 deg. Pin 1 marking: not in the read text, RESEARCH_REQUIRED (many arrays show no top mark and use a beveled or notched corner or a printed dot, unverified).

FCO origin for the 9 mm vertical parts: bbox of pin centers and mounting holes center (PTV09: x 0 to 7, y -4.4 to +4.4 about pin 2, hole centers), so origin at (X 3.5 from the pin row toward the shaft, Y 0 = pin 2). The shaft axis is then 4.0 from the origin (toward the shaft side).

For PCB-mount (RV16AF "PCB mount" listings) pins are on a 2.5 x ... pitch NOT established.

**Orientation (OHMNI default):** shaft along +Z (vertical, up) for vertical PCB mounting; pins in a row along Y, pin 1 at +Y; shaft axis at X = 0, Y = 0. RESEARCH_REQUIRED: terminal spacing and footprint of both families; right-angle variants not covered.

# [OHM-010] Axial carbon-film resistor
## Identity
- Canonical name: Axial carbon-film resistor. ID OHM-010, slug `res_axial_carbon_film`.
- Category: passive / resistor. Physical package: axial leaded cylinder (PKG-AXIAL_RES). Mounting: tht, horizontal.
- Aliases: carbon film resistor, CFR, CF resistor. Variants: 1/6 W (backlog "1/8 W"), 1/4 W, 1/2 W, 1 W, 2 W.
- Class B, priority P1, complexity 2. De facto package (no standard confirmed).
## Physical Dimensions
Family table in PKG-AXIAL_RES, Yageo CFR rows. OHMNI default member AX_1_4W (CFR-25): L 6.3 (5.8 to 6.8), D 2.4 (2.2 to 2.6), lead d 0.55 (0.50 to 0.60), pitch P 10.16 (DERIVED, UNCERTAIN, min 7.62), lead tail bottom Z = -2.6. Other rows: CFR-12 3.4 x 1.9 d0.45 P7.62; CFR-50 9.0 x 3.3 d0.55 P12.70; CFR-100 11.5 x 4.5 d0.8 P15.24; CFR-200 15.5 x 5.0 d0.8 P20.32. Body overall height above board = D (body rests on board), overall length = P + d.
## Geometry
Cylinder along X on the board plane (bottom tangent at Z=0), two formed leads bent 90 deg down to the PCB. Body ends slightly shouldered (LOD2). Four color bands wrapped around the body.
## Leads / Pins / Terminals
2 round wire leads, dia 0.55, tinned copper-clad steel/copper (material not stated in sources; MAT_TIN_BRIGHT as visual default), bend radius 1.0*d inner, vertical segment at X = +/-P/2, down to Z=-2.6 (PCB penetration 2.6 - 0 = 2.6 below Z=0). Numbering: pin 1 at -X (-P/2, 0), pin 2 at +X (+P/2, 0). Non-polar.
## PCB Interface
Two holes dia = d + 0.3 to 0.5 (footprint choice, not sourced; default 0.9 for d=0.55) at (+/-P/2, 0). FCO origin = midpoint of the two holes = body center. standoff 0, body_offset (0, 0).
## Materials
Body MAT_RESISTOR_PAINT_BEIGE (proposed token). Leads MAT_TIN_BRIGHT. Bands MAT_BAND_* decals.
## Appearance
Carbon film body is typically beige/tan (de facto convention, not in the opened datasheets: Yageo CFR sheet describes only a 4-band code). 4 bands: digit, digit, multiplier, tolerance (gold = 5 % J, red = 2 % G per Yageo). Gloss low-medium. Manufacturer variation: tan to light brown to green-tan; some printed body markings on larger sizes.
## Orientation Markings
Not polarized. Reading direction: first band nearest terminal 1 (-X); tolerance band at the +X end with a larger gap.
## Recognition Features
1. Cylinder with narrow leads bent at 90 deg to PCB. 2. Distinct color bands incl. gap before tolerance band. 3. Aspect ratio L/D about 2.6. 4. Beige body, tin leads.
## Parametric Variants
Safe: rated_power row, L, D, d, P, band_count (4 default), band digits (decal). Coupled: P >= L + 4d; lead axis Z = D/2.
## Recommended Base Geometry
Cylinder + 2 leads each as 3 segments (horizontal stub, bend arc, vertical tube); band cylinders (thin sleeves, radius D/2 + 0.01).
## Modeling Procedure
1. Choose member row. 2. Place cylinder axis at (0,0,D/2), length L. 3. Create each lead: horizontal tube from body end to X = +/-P/2 at Z=D/2, apply bend, vertical tube down to Z=-2.6. 4. Add 4 band sleeves at the fractional positions of PKG-AXIAL_RES. 5. Assign materials.
## LOD Strategy
LOD0: cylinder + two lead boxes/tubes (no bend radius, no bands). LOD1: bands as colored sleeves or decal, bend as chamfered segment, lead full length. LOD2: bend radius arcs, end shoulders/caps, lead end chamfer.
## Simplification Rules
May omit: end shoulders, bend radius (LOD0/1), lead end chamfer. Never omit: both leads, body cylinder, lead bend/vertical, band count (>= tolerance band separated).

# [OHM-012] Cement power resistor
## Identity
- Canonical name: Cement power resistor. ID OHM-012, slug `res_power_cement`.
- Category passive / resistor. Package PKG-POWER_RES (cement style). Mounting tht, horizontal.
- Aliases: cement resistor, SQP, ceramic encased wirewound, "sand cast". Variants: 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 15, 20 W.
- Class A, priority P2, complexity 3.
## Physical Dimensions
OHMNI default CEM_5W (Yageo SQP500): L 22 (20.5 to 23.5), W 9.5 (8.5 to 10.5), H 9.0 (8.0 to 10.0), lead d 0.8 (0.75 to 0.85), pitch P 25.40 (DERIVED, UNCERTAIN). Overall height H, overall width W. Full member table: PKG-POWER_RES.
## Geometry
Rectangular block with flat faces (width W along Y, height H along Z, length L along X), resting on the board (bottom at Z=0), sharp edges with small 0.3 mm round-over (LOD2, de facto). Leads exit end face centers at Z = H/2 and extend horizontally then bend down. A shallow white-ish printed marking field on the side face.
## Leads / Pins / Terminals
2 round leads d 0.8, tinned (visual MAT_TIN_BRIGHT, material not stated in opened sources). Horizontal stub from the end face to X = +/-P/2 at Z = H/2 (4.5), bend 90 deg, vertical down to Z = -2.6. Pin 1 (-P/2, 0), pin 2 (+P/2, 0). Non-polar. Note total vertical drop from lead axis to tail = H/2 + 2.6 = 7.1.
## PCB Interface
Holes dia 1.2 (footprint choice, not sourced). Body centered on the pad pattern. Standoff 0 (real cement resistors are often mounted raised for cooling; parameter standoff 0 to 5, UNCERTAIN).
## Materials
Body MAT_CERAMIC_ALUMINA_WHITE (cement white to light cream), leads MAT_TIN_BRIGHT, print MAT_SILKSCREEN_WHITE or black ink (#151517 decal).
## Appearance
Cement/ceramic block, off-white to cream, with black printed text. Example marking from Yageo: "YAGEO 1801 10WN 100R J" (brand, date code, power + N, value, tolerance). Some brands use beige or pale pink; matte rough surface (roughness 0.8).
## Orientation Markings
Not polarized. Text reads along +X on the +Z (top) face and, in many brands, on one side face; no pin marking.
## Recognition Features
1. Rectangular white block with axial leads from end centers, 2. printed power/value text, 3. high block compared to lead diameter, 4. leads bent down at spaced pitch.
## Parametric Variants
rated_power row (2 to 20 W), standoff, pitch, text. Coupled: P >= L + 4d; lead axis Z = H/2 + standoff.
## Recommended Base Geometry
Box + two cylinders each lead composed of 3 segments; text decal plane.
## Modeling Procedure
1. Box centered X=0,Y=0, Z from standoff to standoff+H. 2. Add lead from end face center to X=+/-P/2. 3. Bend down to Z=-2.6. 4. Decal print on top face. 
## LOD Strategy
LOD0: box + 2 lead boxes. LOD1: box with round-over minimal, leads with bend, text decal. LOD2: round-over fillets, lead bend arcs, slight end-face lead recess ring (de facto).
## Simplification Rules
May omit round-over, text. Never omit: block proportions (L,W,H), lead height at H/2, both leads, drop to PCB.

Ceramic-tube cylinder with metal end caps slightly narrower than the coating, silicone coating over the winding; axis along X at Z = C/2. Leads exit end cap centers, same formed-lead scheme as axial resistors.

2 round leads d 1.02, tinned copper (datasheet: tin or tin/lead-coated copper terminals) on stainless steel end caps. Pin 1 (-P/2, 0), pin 2 (+P/2, 0). Tail Z = -2.6.

Not polarized. Printed text along the length.

LOD0: cylinder + 2 leads. LOD1: end caps, formed leads, text decal. LOD2: bend radius, coating ends, cap chamfer.

# [OHM-014] SMD current-sense resistor
## Identity
- Canonical name: SMD current-sense resistor (metal strip). ID OHM-014, slug `res_smd_current_sense`.
- Category passive / resistor. Package: instance/variant of PKG-CHIP2T (owned by G01; this entry documents only deltas and extra sizes). Mounting smd.
- Aliases: shunt chip resistor, metal strip resistor, Power Metal Strip (Vishay WSL/WSK), low-ohmic chip, Kelvin sense resistor. Variants: 2-terminal 0603 to 2816; 4-terminal Kelvin WSK1206 and WSK2512.
- Class C, priority P1, complexity 2.
- Imperial and metric names: 0603 (1608), 0805 (2012), 1206 (3216), 2010 (5025), 2512 (6432). Vishay's metal-strip bodies are SLIGHTLY different from thick-film chips (e.g., Vishay "0603" L 1.52 vs thick-film 1.6).
## Physical Dimensions
Source: Vishay WSL "Power Metal Strip Resistors, Low Value", doc 30100, revision 23-Nov-2023 (inches in the datasheet, converted by the datasheet to mm as shown). T = terminal length measured along L at each end (as read; Vishay "T").

| Size | L | W | H | T (terminal length) | Basis/Conf |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0603 | 1.52 +/-0.254 | 0.76 +/-0.254 | 0.406 +/-0.127 | 0.381 +/-0.254 | MFR_DATASHEET, M |
| 0805 | 2.03 +/-0.254 | 1.27 +/-0.254 | 0.406 +/-0.127 | 0.381 +/-0.254 | M |
| 1206 | 3.20 +/-0.254 | 1.60 +/-0.254 | 0.64 to 1.04 (varies by resistance range, 0.025 to 0.041 in) | 1.04 +/-0.254 | M |
| 2010 | 5.08 +/-0.254 | 2.54 +/-0.254 | 0.51 or 0.64 +/-0.254 (0.020 or 0.025 in) | 1.47 +/-0.254 | M |
| 2512 (OHMNI DEFAULT) | 6.35 +/-0.254 | 3.18 +/-0.254 | 0.64 to 0.76 +/-0.254 (0.025 to 0.030 in, varies) | 2.72 +/-0.254 | M |
| 2816 | 7.1 +/-0.254 | 4.2 +/-0.254 | 0.64 or 1.57 +/-0.254 (0.025 or 0.062 in) | 2.49 +/-0.254 | M |

OHMNI default: 2512, H 0.70 (mid of the stated range), T 2.72. **0612 wide-terminal ("reverse geometry") size, gap-fill (two manufacturers, which disagree slightly).** Terminals are on the two LONG sides, so the terminal-to-terminal span is the SHORT axis. OHMNI maps the short axis to X (terminal axis) and the long axis to Y.

| Source | X span (terminal to terminal) | Y (terminal width) | H | Terminal length along X |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vishay WSL0612 (opened farnell.com/datasheets/2049198.pdf; the Vishay-hosted rev was not readable) | 1.50 +/-0.127 | 3.05 +/-0.127 | 0.381 +/-0.127 | T 0.381 +/-0.254 |
| Yageo PE0612 (PE0612FKF070R1L spec sheet, "SMD Wide Termination", 2 terminals) | L 1.6 +/-0.2 | W 3.2 +/-0.2 | T 0.6 +/-0.15 | B1 0.3 +/-0.15 (reading of B1 not confirmed) |

Vishay solder-pad letters a 0.76, b 1.98, c 3.40: a (0.76) matches the inter-terminal window W - 2T = 1.50 - 0.762 = 0.74, so a = pad gap and c = pad width along Y (3.40 > 3.05); b = 1.98 is read as the pad-to-pad outer span (INFERRED). OHMNI default for the 0612 variant: Vishay numbers (X 1.50, Y 3.05, H 0.38, T 0.38), terminal centers at X = +/-(1.50 - 0.381)/2 = +/-0.56. The Yageo part is 0.1 to 0.2 mm larger in each direction and 0.2 mm thicker (both within each other's tolerance band on length and width; H differs 0.38 vs 0.6, not reconciled, so H range 0.38 to 0.6). Basis MFR_DATASHEET, confidence M for L/W, L for H and T.

**4-terminal 0612 (Yageo PS0612, spec sheet PS0612FKG070R01L, opened).** "SMD Four Termination", L 1.6 +0.15/-0.2, W 3.2 +/-0.2, T 0.6 +/-0.2, B1 2.2 +/-0.2, B2 0.5, B3 0.5, B4 0.45, B5 0.7 (each +/-0.2). The read said the terminals are on the long sides (two per side). Which of B1..B5 is the sense-terminal spacing, the current-terminal width, or the gap could NOT be established from text (no drawing view). Plausible reading (UNVERIFIED): B1 2.2 = length of the wide current terminal along Y, with a 0.5 mm sense terminal beside it; do not implement from this reading without a drawing. Vishay WSK0612 was not retrievable (vishay.com/docs/30196/wsk0612.pdf = 404; TTI product page has no dimensions).

**3-terminal variants:** no opened document describes a 3-terminal current-sense chip (Vishay WSLT2512, doc 30121, opened, turned out to be a 2-terminal part with L 6.35, W 3.18, H 0.635, T 0.762, pads a 1.65, b 3.68, l 4.06). OHMNI treats "3-terminal" as the 4-terminal part with the two sense terminals on one side merged; RESEARCH_REQUIRED, not specified further.

**Cross-check of WSL2512 (re-read in gap-fill pass):** L 6.35, W 3.18; H = 0.635 (0.5 to 0.99 mOhm), 2.21 (1 to 4.9 mOhm, as read, implausibly tall: likely a table scramble), 1.19 (5 to 6.9 mOhm), 0.762 (7 mOhm to 0.5 Ohm); the H values in the first-pass table (0.64 to 0.76) agree for the common ranges; solder pad a 3.05, b 3.68 to 4.06, l 1.27 (read; roles not established). WSL2512 T = 2.72 only for 0.5 to 0.99 mOhm in this read; first-pass T for other ranges not re-confirmed, so T 2.72 is valid for the lowest-ohm range only. Treat the default T 2.72 as range-dependent (L).
4-terminal Kelvin (Vishay WSK, opened): WSK1206 (doc 30195, rev 15-Dec-2023): L 3.20 +/-0.254, W 1.60 +/-0.254, H 0.635 +/-0.254, T 0.508 +/-0.254, terminal dims A 0.584 +/-0.254 and B 0.457 +/-0.254. WSK2512 (doc 30108, rev 11-Dec-2023): L 6.35 +/-0.254, W 3.18 +/-0.254, H 0.635 +/-0.254, T 2.66 (0.105 in) for 0.5 to 0.99 milliohm, A 0.762 / 2.21 / 1.19 for 0.5 to 0.99 / 1 to 4.9 / 5 to 200 milliohm ranges, B 0.508. The datasheets label current connections I1, I2 and voltage sense connections E1, E2. WHICH edges carry E1/E2 and the exact terminal geometry could NOT be determined from the read text, so the 4-terminal 3D layout is RESEARCH_REQUIRED (pad table values returned: WSK1206 a 1.01, b 1.778, c 0.762, d 0.254, l 1.778; WSK2512 a,b 2.29, c,d 3.68, e 0.76, l 1.70 for 5 to 200 milliohm; their roles were not established).
## Geometry
Delta from PKG-CHIP2T: the body is a flat metal strip (resistive alloy, visible as metallic center) with copper terminals wrapped at the ends; the center top carries a dark protective coating. Terminal length T is much longer than a thick-film chip's end cap (for 2512: 2.72 vs. typical about 0.5 to 0.6), so the exposed center "window" is only L - 2T (2512: 0.91 mm). No glass/alumina substrate visible; height H is the strip plus coat. Overall: box L x W x H, terminals on both ends. (Thick-film 2512 chip numbers must come from G01's table; not restated here.)
## Leads / Pins / Terminals
2 terminals, flat pads wrapping the end faces, length T along X, width W, pad underside at Z=0. Pin 1 at -X: center (-(L - T)/2, 0) = (-1.815, 0) for 2512. Pin 2 at (+1.815, 0). 4-terminal: RESEARCH_REQUIRED (see above). 0612 wide-terminal variant: 2 terminals on the long sides, terminal centers at X = +/-0.56, each terminal 0.381 long (X) by 3.05 wide (Y).
## PCB Interface
SMD pads; recommended pad lengths longer than chip (Vishay layout tables exist in the sheets but were not parsed unambiguously). Origin FCO = center of the pad pair = body center. standoff 0.
## Materials
Terminals MAT_TIN_MATTE (solder-plated copper), center element MAT_ALLOY_MANGANIN (proposed), top coating MAT_RESISTOR_COAT_BLACK. Wide/long terminals are MAT_TIN_MATTE up the end faces.
## Appearance
Dark strip center with bright tin-colored large end blocks; laser mark on top coat (value, e.g. "R010"); manufacturer color varies (some have bare metallic strip top). Decal only.
## Orientation Markings
Not polarized. 4-terminal variants have orientation implied by sense terminals (RESEARCH_REQUIRED).
## Recognition Features
1. Very large terminals relative to body (about 40 % of length each at 2512), 2. low profile, 3. short dark center window, 4. (WSK) extra small terminals.
## Parametric Variants
size (0603..2816), H, T, terminal_count (2 now; 4 RESEARCH_REQUIRED). Coupled: L - 2T > 0.3 (window); H within range for size.
## Recommended Base Geometry
Box (center) + two end boxes (terminals) + thin top coat box.
## Modeling Procedure
1. Create strip box L x W x H*0.7 at Z = H*0.15 (center). 2. Terminals: box T x W x H at both ends, bottom Z=0. 3. Top coat box on the center, thickness 0.05. 4. Decal marking.
## LOD Strategy
LOD0: a single box L x W x H. LOD1: terminals and center distinct. LOD2: terminal edge chamfers 0.05, coat inset.
## Simplification Rules
May omit: laser mark, edge chamfers. Never omit: long terminals (T proportion) and the center window.

# [OHM-015] Metal shunt resistor
## Identity

## Physical Dimensions
Default style: bolt-on (Vishay WSBS8518...35 reference, gap-fill corrected, see PKG-SHUNT): overall length 85 +/-0.41 (M; the first-pass value 60 was the hole spacing), width 18 +/-0.20 (M), thickness 3.00 +/-0.05 (M), bolt hole dia 7 +/-0.10 (M), hole center spacing 60 (M-L, from sibling sheet 30134 only; positions X = +/-30), element length A 15.62 for 500 micro-ohm (B 17.65; A/B vary with resistance), sense pin spacing 9 +/-0.25 (M, axis unresolved). Blocks: copper, (85 - 17.65)/2 = 33.7 long each; chamfer 1.98 x 45 deg typ. OHMNI placeholders: sense pin dia 1.0 (L), sense pin length below strip 3.0 (L). RESEARCH_REQUIRED: sense pin axis/offset and length. Alternate SMD style (Isabellenhutte BVS 3920): L 10 (+0.3), W 5.2 (+0.3/-0.2), H 0.5 +/-0.1, land: l 11, w 6.2, a 2.7, x 5.6 (roles unresolved).
## Geometry
Flat strip along X: two terminal blocks (copper) at the ends with a bolt hole each, a central resistive element (alloy) of the same thickness but visibly different color, and a small mark. Welded seam lines (ISA-WELD / welded terminal to element) at the block/element boundaries (LOD2). Two thin sense pins protrude from the underside near the element ends (WSBS has "integrated sense pins").
## Leads / Pins / Terminals
4 connection features: pins 1 and 2 = bolt holes dia 7 (terminal blocks, at X = -30 and +30, Y=0; c-c 60); pins 3 and 4 = sense pins at (-4.5, 0) and (+4.5, 0) going down (THT, dia 1.0, length 3.0, UNCERTAIN). Numbering: 1 at -X, 2 at +X, 3 at -X sense, 4 at +X sense. Terminal material copper (tinned/ nickel plated per brand, unverified).
## PCB Interface
Sense pins THT holes dia 1.4 at (+/-4.5, 0); bolt holes through-board only if mounted to busbar (not modeled; the model has holes in the terminal blocks only). FCO origin: bbox of holes = X extent +/-30 (bolt holes) with pins inside, so origin at strip center. Body overhangs the hole pattern by 12.5 each end. Standoff default 0 (strip bottom at Z=0); real mounting heights UNCERTAIN.
## Materials
Terminal blocks MAT_COPPER, element MAT_ALLOY_MANGANIN (proposed), sense pins MAT_TIN_BRIGHT.
## Appearance
Copper blocks with a darker center; markings (value, tolerance, type) engraved on the element face; some brands tin or nickel plate the blocks.
## Orientation Markings
Not polarized; 4-terminal sense pins implied by position.
## Recognition Features
1. Long thick flat strip, 2. two bolt holes, 3. contrasting center element, 4. two small sense pins.
## Parametric Variants
style (bolt_on|smd_3920), L, W, thickness, hole_dia, hole_center_from_end, sense_pin_spacing. Coupled: hole_center_from_end >= hole_dia/2 + 2; element_length = L - 2*terminal_block_length.
## Recommended Base Geometry
Box strip (3 segments by material), 2 cylindrical hole cuts, 2 pin cylinders.
## Modeling Procedure
1. Strip box 85 x 18 x 3. 2. Split into blocks (33.7 each) and element (17.65, with 15.62 resistive part); assign materials. 3. Cut holes dia 7 at +/-30. 4. Add 2 sense pins. 5. Optional weld seam grooves.
## LOD Strategy
LOD0: single box. LOD1: three-material strip, holes, pins. LOD2: seam grooves, hole chamfers, engraved text.
## Simplification Rules
May omit: seams, text, chamfers. Never omit: bolt holes, strip proportions, sense pins if the 4-wire variant is used.

type (convex|concave), terminal count per side n, element size (0402|0603|1206), pitch, W1. Coupled: (n-1)*P + W1 <= L; W2 = 2*H + gap (gap >= 0.2).
## Recommended Base Geometry
Box body + n*2 terminal boxes (convex) or box with cut notches filled by terminal inlays (concave).
## Modeling Procedure
1. Body box L x W x T centered, bottom Z=0. 2. Top coat plate (0.05). 3. For each side X sign s, for i in 0..n-1: terminal box W1 x H x T_term at (s*(W/2 - H/2), Y_i), convex bulge +0.02 or concave notch radius W1/2. 4. Assign pin numbers.
## LOD Strategy
LOD0: single box. LOD1: body + 8 terminals. LOD2: bulge/notch details, overcoat inset.
## Simplification Rules
May omit: bulge, overcoat edge. Never omit: terminal count, row pitch, pin-1 reference.
