# [OHM-099] TO-247 power transistor
## Identity
- Canonical name: TO-247 power transistor (TO-247-3); ID OHM-099, slug `transistor_to247`; semiconductor; PKG-TO247; THT
- Aliases: TO-247-3, TO247, TO-247AC / TO-247AD (Vishay outline names), SOT429 (Nexperia code)
- Variants: TO-247-3 with two outlines (AD default, AC older); TO-247-4 and TO-3P are PROPOSED ADDITIONS (OHM-201, OHM-202).
- Class A, P1, complexity 3.
## Physical Dimensions
Per PKG-TO247 (default outline AD): width 15.9 (X), height 20.95 (Z, tab top to lead shoulder), thickness 5.02 (Y), pitch 5.45, mounting hole 3.6 at 6.17 below the tab top, hole dish 7.2, lead thickness 0.6, tail widths 1.2 / 2.0. AC outline: 15.7 x 20.5 x 4.95, hole 5.5 below top. M for envelope and hole diameter, M-L for the hole position and tab thickness.
## Geometry
Upright slab with a metal tab on the back (+Y). The tab is 14.0 wide (Vishay E1, optional thermal-pad contour) and its exposed back runs from about 4.4 above the lead shoulder to the top. A Ø3.6 hole passes through the tab and the plastic, centered 6.17 below the tab top, with a Ø7.2 circular dish (depth not sourced; cosmetic 0.5) in the plastic front around it. Interim plastic height: plastic top at about tab top minus 2.6 (L, derived from hole dish geometry). The first-pass plastic height 14.0 is withdrawn: it was derived from Nexperia E1, which Vishay documents show is the thermal-pad contour width (13.5-14.2), not a height.
## Leads / Pins / Terminals
Pins at x = -5.45, 0, +5.45, y = 0 (lead plane about the body thickness mid-plane: A1 2.41 against A/2 2.51). Each lead is a flat strip 0.6 thick with a 1.2 wide tail and a wider shoulder (2.0 wide, b2; a 3.0 wide b4 section also exists and its position is unresolved) over about 4.2 mm (L1) below the plastic; tail truncated to -2.6 (uncut length 15.2 standard, 20.1 long-lead). Pin 2 tied to the tab. Tin plated.
## PCB Interface
THT, three holes at 5.45 pitch. Standoff default 0. body_offset (0, -0.1) (lead plane 2.41 from the back face, 2.61 from the front face; DERIVED, L-M). The tab hole is a body feature and is not in the FCO box.
## Materials
MAT_EPOXY_BLACK plastic; tab MAT_NICKEL (or tin matte); leads MAT_TIN_BRIGHT.
## Appearance
Black body, front marking; silver tab at back.
## Orientation Markings
Tab at +Y; pin 1 at -X.
## Recognition Features
1. Wide 15.9 body, 20.95 tall with the round hole and dish near the top. 2. Three widely spaced leads at 5.45. 3. Tab on rear.
## Parametric Variants
outline {AD default, AC}, lead_length {standard, long}, lead_count (3 now; 4 proposed), isolated option, standoff, dish on/off.
## Recommended Base Geometry
Plastic box + tab plate with hole + stepped leads.
## Modeling Procedure
1. Plastic box 15.9 x 3.03 x (20.95 - 2.6), y from -2.61 to +0.41. 2. Tab plate y in [+0.41, +2.41] (2.0 thick for AD, 1.27-1.5 for AC), full height to Z = 20.95, 14.0 wide above Z = 4.4 and plastic-wrapped below. 3. Hole Ø3.6 at Z = 20.95 - 6.17 through all Y; Ø7.2 dish in the front plastic. 4. Leads. 5. Decals.
## LOD Strategy
LOD0 two boxes + leads; LOD1 hole, dish, shoulders; LOD2 chamfers/radii.
## Simplification Rules
Never omit hole, tab, three leads at 5.45. May omit lead shoulder steps and the dish.

# [OHM-100] DPAK / TO-252
## Identity
- Canonical name: DPAK / TO-252 (3-terminal, one lead cropped); ID OHM-100, slug `dpak_to252`; semiconductor / power MOSFET, regulator, diode; PKG-DPAK; SMD
- Aliases: DPAK, TO-252, TO-252AA (Vishay doc 95627/71197 titles), SOT428, DPAK-3 (onsemi 369AA), TO-252-3
- Naming note: TO-252 and DPAK are the same package; D2PAK (OHM-101) is TO-263 and larger. IPAK/TO-251 is through-hole.
- Class A, P1, complexity 3.
## Physical Dimensions
Per PKG-DPAK: plastic 6.10 (X) x 6.58 (Y) x 2.29 (Z), pitch 2.29, tab-tip to lead-tip 9.91, tab 5.33 wide at the tip and about 1.1 beyond the plastic, tab thickness 0.6, standoff 0.08. CONSENSUS (H) for the plastic envelope; M-L for the tab extension and Z structure.
## Geometry
Plastic block 6.10 x 6.58 x 2.29 whose bottom sits about 0.08 above the seating plane. A metal tab (about 0.6 thick) is embedded in it, with its underside exposed (Vishay D1 x E1 minimum mounting surface 5.21 x 4.32) and a 5.33-wide end that protrudes about 1.08 past the +Y plastic edge. Two gull-wing leads leave the -Y face about mid height and run about 2.25 mm beyond the plastic, ending in a 1.59 foot. The center lead is cropped to a stub of 0 to 1.02 mm (default: omitted).
## Leads / Pins / Terminals
Pin 1 (-2.29, -4.1), pin 3 (+2.29, -4.1); lead 0.78 wide, 0.52 thick, foot 1.59; middle lead cropped (default omitted; optional stub protruding up to 1.0 from the plastic, Vishay L4 max 1.02). Tab = pin 2/4.
## PCB Interface
SMD pads: lead pads 1.06 x 2.60 at pitch 4.572, tab pad 5.632 x 5.70, total 10.70 (Diodes). Standoff 0.08 (plastic belly above the tab underside; tab bottom and feet at Z = 0). Tab tip y = +4.955, lead tip y = -4.955 (9.91 span, FCO centered). Plastic y in [-2.705, +3.875]. Body bbox (plastic + tab) center (0, +1.13) DERIVED.
## Materials
Plastic MAT_EPOXY_BLACK; tab/leads MAT_TIN_MATTE.
## Appearance
Black body with 2-3 line marking; matte silver tab visible at the +Y end and on the underside.
## Orientation Markings
Tab on +Y; pin 1 at -X. A 45-degree plastic chamfer may appear (Nexperia note on SOT428 NXP table).
## Recognition Features
1. Two leads plus big tab on opposite side. 2. Stubby 6.1 x 6.6 footprint. 3. Exposed tab at the +Y end.
## Parametric Variants
stub_length 0-1.02 (default 0), tab width, standoff 0-0.13, 5-lead variant (RESEARCH_REQUIRED).
## Recommended Base Geometry
Box + plate + bent strips.
## Modeling Procedure
1. Tab plate Z 0..0.6, from y = -2.705 to +4.955 (5.33 wide at the tip, widening to the plastic width inside; taper not sourced). 2. Plastic block 6.10 x 6.58, Z 0.08..2.29, y -2.705..+3.875. 3. Two leads from the plastic -Y face (Z about 1.2) bending down to feet at Z 0..0.52, tips at y = -4.955. 4. Optional stub. 5. Decal.
## LOD Strategy
LOD0 box + tab + two feet; LOD1 gull-wing leads, tab narrowing; LOD2 chamfer, radii, marking.
## Simplification Rules
Never omit the tab at +Y or the missing center lead. May omit chamfer and stub.

lead_count {3 cropped, 5}, tab extension, stub, standoff 0-0.25.
## Recommended Base Geometry
Box + plate + bent strips.
## Modeling Procedure
1. Tab plate 10 wide (tab taper not sourced) from y = -2.85 to +7.65, Z 0..1.4. 2. Plastic block 10 x 9.0, Z 0.1..4.3, y -2.85..+6.15 (tab embedded, bottom exposed). 3. Leads from plastic -Y face (Z about 2.2) bending down to feet at Z 0..0.55, tips at y = -7.65. 4. Decal.
## LOD Strategy
LOD0 boxes + feet; LOD1 gull-wing leads, tab; LOD2 chamfers, radii, tab taper.
## Simplification Rules
Never omit tab, cropped middle lead, thermal tab underside. May omit stub.

# [OHM-102] PowerPAK SO-8 MOSFET
## Identity
- Canonical name: PowerPAK SO-8 MOSFET (Vishay single); ID OHM-102, slug `powerpak_so8`; semiconductor / power MOSFET; PKG-POWERPAK; SMD
- Aliases: PowerPAK SO-8, PPAK SO-8
- NOT: SO-8FL / DFN5 5x6 (onsemi 488AA), PowerPAK SO-8L, LFPAK, PSOF. See family distinction.
- Class A, P2, complexity 3.
## Physical Dimensions
Per PKG-POWERPAK (Vishay drawing 5881, document 71655, rev 13-Feb-17, now read in the official Vishay datasheets Si7898DP and SiR180DP): overall 6.15 (X, across leads) x 5.15 (Y), molded body 5.89 (X, E1) x 4.90 (Y, D1) x 1.04 (Z), e 1.27, lead b 0.41, c 0.28, L 0.61, exposed drain pad 3.76 (Y) x 3.66 (X). Recommended land pattern (Vishay Application Note 826 as reproduced in the datasheet page): overall 6.61 x 4.42, drain pad 3.91 x 3.81. M.
## Geometry
Flat low-profile molded block 5.89 x 4.90 x 1.04. Eight flat leads leave the two long (+/-X) faces and protrude only about 0.13 mm beyond the plastic (E 6.15 vs E1 5.89). Exposed copper drain pad 3.76 x 3.66 on the underside, centered; pin-1 marker on top.
## Leads / Pins / Terminals
8 flat leads at 1.27 pitch, 0.41 wide, 0.28 thick, 0.61 long (contact length). Pin 1 (-2.77, +1.905); pins 1-4 down the left side (y = +1.905, +0.635, -0.635, -1.905), pins 5-8 up the right side (pin 5 (+2.77, -1.905) ... pin 8 (+2.77, +1.905)). Pins 1-3 source, 4 gate, 5-8 drain (tied to the pad). Contact center x = 3.075 - 0.61/2 = 2.77 (DERIVED; AN826 pad centers are further out and were not resolved).
## PCB Interface
SMD pads 8 + large drain pad (3.91 x 3.81 land pattern; package pad 3.76 x 3.66). Standoff 0.05 (Vishay A1 nominal; max/min columns scrambled in all three extractions). FCO (0, 0). body_offset (0, 0).
## Materials
MAT_EPOXY_BLACK body; leads MAT_TIN_MATTE; underside pad MAT_COPPER/MAT_TIN_MATTE.
## Appearance
Black body, two-line marking; copper-colored pad visible only on the underside.
## Orientation Markings
Pin 1 dot or chamfer at top-left (-X, +Y).
## Recognition Features
1. SO-8 sized but only 1.04 high. 2. Eight tiny flush leads with no gull-wing reach (0.13 protrusion). 3. Large underside pad.
## Parametric Variants
Dual version (two pads) is NOT modeled here (Vishay drawing 5881 shows a "backside view of dual pad"; dual pad geometry unverified).
## Recommended Base Geometry
Thin box + eight flat strips + underside plate.
## Modeling Procedure
1. Body 5.89 (X) x 4.90 (Y) x 1.04 (Z, from standoff). 2. Eight leads at pitch 1.27, tips at x = +/-3.075. 3. Underside pad plate 3.66 x 3.76. 4. Pin 1 dot.
## LOD Strategy
LOD0 box; LOD1 leads + dot; LOD2 chamfers, exposed pad relief.
## Simplification Rules
Never omit the 8 leads or 1.04 height. May omit pad underside.

Dimensions M, Geometry M (was L), Materials M. Resolved: body vs pad interpretation. E1 5.89 cannot be the exposed pad because the pad is D2 x E2 (3.76 x 3.66) and the AN826 drain land is 3.91 x 3.81, while E1 is only 0.26 below the 6.15 lead-tip span and the AN826 land width 6.61 exceeds 6.15; so D1/E1 are the molded body (plastic 4.90 x 5.89), leads protrude 0.13. ## Convention problems in 00_architecture.md
1. Section 6: SOT-23 appears in the dual-row "rows parallel to Y, pin 1 top-left" rule and in the 3-lead-transistor row with "pins 1-2 on -Y, pin 1 at -X". These are 90 degrees apart. G07 follows the latter.
2. Section 6 says SOT-23 pins "1-2 on the -Y side" which is true for SOT-23-3 only; for -5/-6, pins 1-3 are on -Y. Rewrite as "pins 1..ceil(N/2) on -Y".
3. Tabbed THT: the architecture does not say where the lead plane sits within the body thickness; G07 chose "centered on plastic" for TO-220 (Q 2.60-2.84 roughly supports it) and the body thickness mid-plane for TO-247 (A1 2.41 vs A/2 2.51) and TO-126, and recorded body_offset_mm.
4. Section 4 FCO excludes tab mounting holes from the origin for TO-220/247 (they are not PCB holes); worth stating explicitly.
5. SMD tabbed packages (DPAK, D2PAK) have the tab pad inside the FCO bbox; the YAML `terminals.count` is ambiguous when the tab is a terminal. G07 counts only leads.
6. Cross-group (pass 2): PKG-SOT23 contact |y| values are now stated explicitly (1.0 for 3-lead, 1.2 for 5/6-lead); G05 OHM-070 and G08 OHM-120/121 still carry placeholders pointing at PKG-SOT23 and should copy them.
7. Second pass: PKG-D2PAK and PKG-DPAK Z structure changed (tab embedded, plastic bottom at the standoff, not stacked on the tab); G07 YAML `standoff_mm` for OHM-101 changed from 1.3 to 0.1, and body_offset values changed (OHM-100 (0, 1.13), OHM-101 (0, 2.4), OHM-099 (0, -0.1), OHM-098 (0, 0.64)). Anything in other groups or the assembler that cached the first-pass values must be refreshed.

# G08: Dual-Row ICs (OHM-103 .. OHM-121)

Group conventions: FCO origin (arch Sec. 4), rotation 0 per arch Sec. 6 dual-row rule: rows parallel to Y, row spacing along X, pin 1 at (-X, +Y), counter-clockwise numbering viewed from top (down the left row, up the right row). Exception: OHM-120/121 (SOT-23), see their entries and the convention problem noted in the Research Confidence of OHM-120/121. Z = 0 is the board top. "Pin position" = center of the terminal PCB-contact area (arch Sec. 17.1): lead axis for DIP, foot-flat center for gull wing.

Gull-wing conventions used by GEN-DUAL_GULLWING (all four SMD families): the lead leaves the body side at roughly mid body thickness, runs outward, bends down through a short sloped leg and ends in a flat foot lying on Z=0. `lead_span` (JEDEC "HE"/"H") is the tip-to-tip outer distance across the two rows. `foot_length` is the flat contact length measured from the tip inward. Terminal contact-center x = +-(lead_span/2 - foot_length/2).

New material tokens: none proposed. Uses MAT_EPOXY_BLACK (body), MAT_TIN_MATTE (leads, default; MAT_TIN_BRIGHT acceptable). Laser marks are decals on MAT_EPOXY_BLACK with the #6E6E70 mark tint from arch Sec. 7.

## PACKAGE FAMILY: PKG-DIP

**Generator:** GEN-DIP. Members: DIP-6, 8, 14, 16, 20 (narrow, 7.62 mm (0.300 in) row spacing) and DIP-28, 40 (wide, 15.24 mm (0.600 in) row spacing). Owner of OHM-103..109.

### Shared geometry
- Rectangular molded plastic body (epoxy) with top and bottom draft, resting on its own standoff: body underside is at Z = A1 above the seating plane (A1 min 0.38 mm (0.015 in)); the lead shoulders are what touch the board (Z=0).
- Two rows of flat stamped leads, 2.54 mm (0.100 in) pitch, row spacing eA (lead-center to lead-center) 7.62 mm narrow / 15.24 mm wide.
- Each lead leaves the body side at mid-height, runs outward, then turns down. The upper portion (b1, "shoulder" section) is wide (about 1.0 to 1.8 mm along Y) and runs from the body down to the seating plane (board top, Z=0). Below Z=0 the lead narrows to the tail (b, 0.36 to 0.56 mm along Y) and continues to the tip. Lead stock thickness c (X direction): 0.20 to 0.36 mm narrow, up to 0.38 mm wide.
- Corner leads (pins 1, N/2, N/2+1, N) have a narrower shoulder on some vendor drawings (Renesas notes "corner leads B1" limits of 0.030-0.045 in on the MS-001 sheets and 0.030-0.045 in on the wide sheets; the Renesas wide table gives B1 0.77-1.77 mm overall). Default: model corner shoulders at the same width unless `corner_lead_slim=true` (0.90 mm).
- The pin-1 end of the body carries a semicircular notch centered on the short end face (X=0) and a pin-1 dimple near pin 1. Notch and dimple are common practice. The opened Microchip drawing C04-018 says only that "pin 1 location varies within the hatched area", so exact notch and dimple coordinates are OHMNI defaults (confidence M/L).

## PACKAGE FAMILY: PKG-SOIC

**Generator:** GEN-DUAL_GULLWING. Owner of OHM-110..113.

### Which body class applies to which pin count
- **Narrow body (3.9 mm, 150 mil), JEDEC outline as printed: MS-012** (variation AA for 8-pin in TI NE555 and Renesas M8.15; AB for 14-pin in TI SN74HC00; AC for 16-pin in Renesas M16.15; NXP SOT108-1 and SOT109-1 print MS-012 without a variation): 8, 14 and 16 pins. Default for OHM-110, 111, 112.
- **Wide body (7.5 mm, 300 mil), JEDEC outline as printed: MS-013** (AA for 16-pin in ADI RW-16 and Renesas M16.3; AC for 20-pin in Renesas M20.3; AD for 20-pin in ADI RI-20-1; NXP SOT163-1 prints MS-013): 16W and 20W (24W, 28W exist, out of scope).
- **OHMNI defaults:** SOIC-8 / SOIC-14 / SOIC-16 = narrow body. **SOIC-20 (OHM-113) = SOIC-20W wide body**; no narrow 20-pin outline appears in any opened document. Parameter `body_class` = narrow | wide on OHM-112 gives SOIC-16W (MS-013-AA). Other options: the ADI RI-20-1 "increased creepage" 20-lead wide package (body length 15.40-15.54 mm) is a longer, different outline for isolators and is NOT the default.

### Shared geometry
- Rectangular molded body, flat top, small top/bottom draft (draft angle not given in opened documents; OHMNI default 5 deg, LOD2 only), underside at standoff A1 above Z=0.
- Gull-wing leads, pitch 1.27 mm (0.050 in), exit at about mid-thickness, foot angle 0 to 8 deg allowed (model 0). Lead width b measured near the foot; Renesas M16.3 notes b is measured 0.36 mm above the seating plane.
- Renesas notes that an optional body chamfer h x 45 deg (0.25-0.75 mm, wide) may be present and that a "visual index" is then required if the chamfer is absent.
- Pin-1 dimple: round, OHMNI default diameter 0.6 narrow / 0.9 wide, depth 0.1, near the pin-1 corner.

# [OHM-103] DIP-6 IC

## Identity
- Canonical name: DIP-6 IC
- ID: OHM-103; slug `dip_6`
- Category: ic; Subcategory: dual_in_line
- Physical package: PKG-DIP.DIP-6
- Mounting type: tht
- Aliases: PDIP-6, DIL-6, DIP6
- Common variants: narrow 7.62 mm body; ceramic CERDIP exists (not modelled)
- Class B; priority P1; complexity 2

## Physical Dimensions
Family table: PKG-DIP. Member values restated (mm; imperial controls in sources):
- Pins N = 6; pitch 2.54 (0.100 in) BSC; row spacing eA = 7.62 (0.300 in) BSC, class narrow (300 mil); shoulder-to-shoulder E 7.62-8.25; eB max 10.92.
- Body length D default 7.12 (6.82-7.42), basis MFR_DRAWING (Vishay 4N35 6-pin DIP package dimensions 7.12 +/-0.3, rev 01-Jan-2026; onsemi 4N35 outlines titled 'PDIP6 7.12x6.50, 2.54P'), confidence M. Body width E1 default 6.50 (6.20-6.80), same two documents, M (the MS-001 family value 6.35 (6.10-7.11) is consistent). Superseded first-pass D 9.27 (8-pin value, a placeholder). Body thickness A2 default 3.3 (2.93-4.95); A max 5.33; A1 (underside to seating plane) 0.38 min.
- Lead: tail length below shoulder L default 3.30 (2.93-3.81); tail width b 0.46 (0.36-0.56); shoulder width b1 1.52 (1.15-1.77); thickness c 0.25 (0.20-0.36).
- JEDEC outline: neither 6-pin document prints a JEDEC number in the extraction; no JEDEC number cited (MS-001 sheets for 8/14/16/20 pins are the nearest reference).
- Height note: the Vishay 6-pin drawing callouts also include 4.5 +/-0.3 (twice), 3.5 +/-0.3, 2.8 +/-0.15, 1.2 +/-0.1 (shoulder-like), 0.5 +/-0.1 (tail width-like), 0.25 (lead thickness-like), 7.62 typ and 7.62 to 9.5 typ (row spacing and lead-tip span). The assignment of 4.5, 3.5, 2.8 to body thickness, tail and standoff could not be made from the extraction, so overall height stays at the MS-001-based 3.68 default; an optocoupler-style option is overall height 4.5 +/-0.3 (L-M). These callouts come from an optocoupler datasheet; a plain-IC PDIP-6 (e.g. Microchip) drawing was not found (web-search budget exhausted).

## Geometry
Body: rectangular block 7.12 (Y) x 6.50 (X) x 3.3 (Z) from Z = 0.38 to Z = 3.68; top/bottom draft (OHMNI default 5 deg, LOD2). The pin-1 end (+Y end) carries a semicircular notch (radius 1.0, centered X = 0, depth 0.3) and a pin-1 dimple (dia 0.8, depth 0.1) at (-2.17, 2.36); notch/dimple geometry is common practice, not read from an opened drawing (M). Mold-parting line: 0.1 mm step at mid-thickness (LOD2). Body is centered on the lead pattern (body_offset 0,0).
Leads emerge from the long sides at Z about 2.03, run outward to X = +-3.81, bend down; the shoulder (wide section b1) ends at Z = 0 (seating plane); the tail narrows to b and extends below the board.

## Leads / Pins / Terminals
6 leads, 3 per row, flat stamped blades, matte tin over copper alloy. Lead axis x = -3.81 (left row, pins 1..3, y descending from +2.540 in 2.54 steps) and x = +3.81 (right row, pins 4..6, y ascending from -2.540). Pin 1 at (-3.81, +2.540). Shoulder b1 1.52 (corner leads may be narrower); tail b 0.46 x c 0.25; tail tip Z = -2.6 (arch default; the drawing L of about 3.30 would reach -3.30 before clinch or trim). Lead-center span per row 5.08.

## PCB Interface
THT holes at pitch 2.54, row spacing 7.62, N = 6; drill diameter is footprint domain (RESEARCH_REQUIRED here). Body underside at Z = 0.38 (shoulders rest on the board). FCO origin = center of hole pattern = body center. Pin-1 at (-3.81, +2.540). tail_below_board_top_mm 2.6 (default).

## Materials
- Body: MAT_EPOXY_BLACK (alt MAT_EPOXY_DARKGRAY). Leads: MAT_TIN_MATTE (default) or MAT_TIN_BRIGHT. Laser-mark decal tint #6E6E70. No new tokens.

## Appearance
Black to dark gray epoxy, semi-matte; leads bright or matte tin. Laser-marked text (part number, date code, logo) as a decal on the top face, reading along Y. Manufacturer variation: body color, dimple position, surface texture. Notch and dimple are geometry; text is decal.

## Orientation Markings
Semicircular notch at the +Y short end (X=0) AND a dimple near pin 1 at the (-X, +Y) corner; pin 1 top-left at rotation 0, counter-clockwise numbering (left row downward, right row upward).

## Recognition Features
1. Two parallel rows of 3 leads at 2.54 pitch. 2. Row spacing 7.62 (narrow vs wide impression). 3. Long black block with end notch. 4. Wide upper lead shoulder narrowing to a thin tail. 5. Body standoff above the board.

## Parametric Variants
Safe: pin_count (generator accepts even 4-64), row_spacing {7.62, 15.24} (10.16 not researched), body_length, body_thickness, tail_length, corner_lead_slim. Coupled: D >= (N/2 - 1) x 2.54 + b1; eA drives lead X; E1 < eA - c.

## Recommended Base Geometry
Box (body) + notch cylinder cut + dimple; per lead one extruded flat profile (stub, shoulder, tail) mirrored left/right; linear array along Y at 2.54.

## Modeling Procedure
1. Body box centered at origin, Z 0.38..3.68. 2. Cut end notch and dimple at +Y end. 3. Build one lead: stub at mid-thickness from the body side to X = row, shoulder b1 down to Z=0, tail b down to Z=-2.6. 4. Array 3 per row at 2.54; mirror to the right row; number counter-clockwise. 5. Apply materials and marking decal.

## LOD Strategy
LOD0: body box + leads as thin strips (tails may be omitted). LOD1: every lead (shoulder + tail), notch, dimple. LOD2: bend radii (inner about 0.2), body draft, mold-parting step, shoulder taper.

## Simplification Rules
May omit: tails (LOD0), dimple, draft, parting step. NEVER omit: pin-1 notch/dimple orientation cue, row spacing, lead pitch and count, body standoff.

## Appearance
Black epoxy, slightly matte, laser-mark text (part number, date code) as a decal; matte-tin leads. Manufacturer variation: body color (black to dark gray), dimple vs bevel, mark text. Dimple is geometry; text is decal.

## Orientation Markings
Round dimple on the top face near pin 1 (top-left at rotation 0). Some manufacturers use a beveled pin-1 end edge or a molded notch instead; Renesas notes a 'visual index' is required when the optional chamfer is absent. Pin 1 top-left, counter-clockwise numbering.

## Parametric Variants
Safe: pin_count (even), pitch, body_length, body_width, lead_span, standoff, lead_width, foot_length, body_thickness, exposed_pad (bool, off). ## Recommended Base Geometry
Box (body) + dimple; per lead a 3-segment polyline extruded to rectangular section (exit stub, sloped leg, flat foot), mirrored across the Y axis; linear array along Y.

## Modeling Procedure
1. Body box Z 0.18..1.58, centered. 2. Dimple at pin-1 corner. 3. Lead profile: stub from body side at Z 0.88, leg down to Z=0, foot outward to X = H/2. 4. Array 4 per row at 1.27; mirror for the right row; number counter-clockwise from top-left. 5. Apply MAT_EPOXY_BLACK / MAT_TIN_MATTE and marking decal.

## LOD Strategy
LOD0: body box + two merged foot bars. LOD1: individual leads with leg and foot, dimple. LOD2: lead bend radii (about 0.1), draft, parting-line step, edge chamfers.

## Simplification Rules
May omit: draft, parting line, bend radii, dimple (LOD0). NEVER omit: lead count/pitch, lead span (tips outside body), standoff, pin-1 corner cue.

Body block 12.8 (Y) x 7.5 (X) x 2.35 (Z) from Z = 0.2 to Z = 2.55, centered on the pad pattern (body_offset 0,0). Top/bottom draft (OHMNI default 5 deg, LOD2). Black epoxy, slightly matte, laser-mark text (part number, date code) as a decal; matte-tin leads. Manufacturer variation: body color (black to dark gray), dimple vs bevel, mark text. Dimple is geometry; text is decal.

## Orientation Markings
Round dimple on the top face near pin 1 (top-left at rotation 0). Some manufacturers use a beveled pin-1 end edge or a molded notch instead; Renesas notes a 'visual index' is required when the optional chamfer is absent. Pin 1 top-left, counter-clockwise numbering.

1. Two rows of 10 gull-wing leads at 1.27 pitch. 2. Flat black body with pin-1 dimple. 3. Lead span 10.3 vs body width 7.5 (tips protrude 1.40 each side). 4. Visible standoff gap. 5. Row-to-row symmetry.

Safe: pin_count (even), pitch, body_length, body_width, lead_span, standoff, lead_width, foot_length, body_thickness, exposed_pad (bool, off). Coupled: D >= span + b; H > E + 2 x leg run; foot x = H/2 - L/2; pin1_y = (N/2-1) x pitch / 2. alternate: SOIC-20W with increased creepage (ADI RI-20-1, D 15.40-15.54, H not extracted)

## Recommended Base Geometry
Box (body) + dimple; per lead a 3-segment polyline extruded to rectangular section (exit stub, sloped leg, flat foot), mirrored across the Y axis; linear array along Y.

## Modeling Procedure
1. Body box Z 0.2..2.55, centered. 2. Dimple at pin-1 corner. 3. Lead profile: stub from body side at Z 1.38, leg down to Z=0, foot outward to X = H/2. 4. Array 10 per row at 1.27; mirror for the right row; number counter-clockwise from top-left. 5. Apply MAT_EPOXY_BLACK / MAT_TIN_MATTE and marking decal.

## LOD Strategy
LOD0: body box + two merged foot bars. LOD1: individual leads with leg and foot, dimple. LOD2: lead bend radii (about 0.1), draft, parting-line step, edge chamfers.

## Simplification Rules
May omit: draft, parting line, bend radii, dimple (LOD0). NEVER omit: lead count/pitch, lead span (tips outside body), standoff, pin-1 corner cue.

- Common variants: 6-lead IC style
- Class B; priority P0; complexity 2

## Physical Dimensions
Instance of PKG-SOT23 (owner G07, final section as of the second pass 2026-10-02); values copied, not re-derived. SOT23-6 member: body length D 2.9 (2.7-3.1), body width E 1.6 (1.3-1.7), overall height A 1.1 (0.9-1.3), standoff A1 0.05 (0.013-0.10), pitch 0.95, lead-tip span HE 3.0, lead width b 0.38 (0.35-0.50), lead thickness c 0.15 (0.10-0.20), foot length 0.40 (0.35-0.55), lead contact center |y| = 1.2 (range 1.2-1.3; G07 DERIVED from the Diodes SOT26 land pattern 2.4 center-to-center). Basis per G07: CONSENSUS / MFR_DRAWING, confidence M. Cross-check from the ADI RJ-6 drawing: pitch 0.95 BSC; body about 2.80-3.00 x 1.50-1.70; JEDEC MO-178-AB as printed.

## Geometry
Use PKG-SOT23 body and gull-wing geometry unchanged. IC-style deltas only: (1) 6 leads instead of 3 (all six populated); (2) the top face is a laser-mark area with a pin-1 dot/dimple at the pin-1 corner; (3) same-size leads on all populated positions (no wider tab lead); (4) optional beveled/notched pin-1 edge is manufacturer-specific, default none.

## Leads / Pins / Terminals
6 gull-wing leads at 0.95 pitch, three along the -Y side (positions x = -0.95, 0, +0.95) and 3 along the +Y side. Pins: 1 (-0.95, -1.2), 2 (0, -1.2), 3 (+0.95, -1.2), 4 (+0.95, +1.2), 5 (0, +1.2), 6 (-0.95, +1.2). Contact x values are +-0.95 / 0; contact |y| = 1.2 (G07 PKG-SOT23 final). Pin 1 = (-0.95, -1.2). All six positions populated.

## PCB Interface
SMD pads per PKG-SOT23 / footprint domain; FCO = pad-pattern center = body center; body standoff per PKG-SOT23; no thermal pad.

## Materials
- Body: MAT_EPOXY_BLACK (alt MAT_EPOXY_DARKGRAY). Leads: MAT_TIN_MATTE (default) or MAT_TIN_BRIGHT. Laser-mark decal tint #6E6E70. No new tokens.

## Appearance
Black epoxy, matte, laser-marked 1-2 line code (decal). Leads matte tin. Marking text is a decal only. Pin-1 dot (decal or 0.3 mm dimple) near the pin-1 corner. Manufacturer variation: dot vs no dot (many SOT-23 ICs mark pin 1 only by the bottom-left lead position and the text orientation).

## Orientation Markings
Pin 1 at the (-X, -Y) bottom-left corner when text reads upright (top view, +X right, +Y up): leads 1,2,3 along the bottom, counter-clockwise numbering (arch Sec. 6, 3-lead/SOT-23 rule). The ADI RJ-6 drawing labels pin 1 ('PIN 1 INDICATOR' printed on RJ-6).

## Recognition Features
1. 6 leads in 3 + 3 arrangement. 2. 0.95 pitch. 3. Pin-1 dot at bottom-left. 4. Small black body with all six positions populated.

## Parametric Variants
Parameters inherited from PKG-SOT23 plus pin_count in {5, 6} and mark_dot (bool). Coupled: lead positions on 0.95 grid; pin 5 omitted when N=5.

## Recommended Base Geometry
Instance PKG-SOT23 generator with lead mask; add pin-1 dimple.

## Modeling Procedure
1. Instantiate PKG-SOT23 body. 2. Place leads at x = -0.95, 0, +0.95 on -Y side; on +Y side at +0.95, 0, -0.95. 3. Add dimple at pin 1. 4. Apply materials, decal.

## LOD Strategy
LOD0: PKG-SOT23 LOD0 with lead mask. LOD1: individual leads, dot. LOD2: per PKG-SOT23 LOD2.

## Simplification Rules
May omit: dimple, draft. NEVER omit: lead count/positions (5 vs 6), pin-1 corner.

# G09: Quad, Leadless, Grid-Array ICs (OHM-122 to OHM-140)

Group G09. Families owned: PKG-QFP, PKG-QFN, PKG-DFN, PKG-PLCC, PKG-BGA, PKG-WLCSP. Evidence level: outline drawings were read through a text-extraction fetch tool (Section 17 item 7); several tables had scrambled columns and only cross-checked values are used. Drawings were not inspected visually.

## PACKAGE FAMILY: PKG-QFP

**Generator:** GEN-QUAD_GULLWING. **Members:** QFP-32 (OHM-122), TQFP-44 (123), TQFP-64 (124), TQFP-100 (125), LQFP-144 (126). All class B.

### Shared geometry
Square plastic body with gull-wing leads on all four sides, N/4 leads per side. Body is a flat slab (top and bottom faces parallel to the PCB) with vertical or slightly drafted sides. Each lead leaves the body side wall at roughly mid-thickness, runs outward, bends down (shoulder), then bends outward again into a flat foot that lies on the PCB. The foot tip defines the lead-tip span D1 (JEDEC-style HD/HE in NXP drawings). Foot contact length is L (0.45 to 0.75 in every opened drawing that states it).

Height classes seen in opened drawings (all cited as "JEDEC MS-026" only as printed in the NXP outline sheets; MS-026 text itself was NOT opened):
- **LQFP (low profile):** body thickness A2 = 1.4 (1.35-1.45), seated height A max 1.6. NXP SOT313-2, SOT314-2, SOT407-1, SOT486-1; Renesas PLQP0100KN-A (14x14, height 1.6, 0.5 pitch).
- **TQFP (thin):** body thickness A2 = 1.0 (0.95-1.05), seated height A max 1.2. NXP SOT376-1, SOT357-1, SOT386-1; Microchip C04-074-PT (7x7x1.0 body).
- **QFP (plain, thick):** Renesas 44-pin QFP (10x10, 0.8 pitch, code S44GB-80-3B4-3) has a lead-tip span of 13.2 +/-0.4 and lead length 1.6 +/-0.2, versus 12.0 (11.85-12.15) tip span and foot 0.45-0.75 on the 10x10 TQFP-44. So plain QFP is the "wide-skirt" style (leads extend ~1.6 mm beyond the body on each side); LQFP/TQFP are the compact style (leads extend ~1.0 mm). Plain-QFP body thickness was not legible in the extracted text: RESEARCH_REQUIRED (not needed by any OHM entry).
- Same body footprint and pitch are used across LQFP and TQFP (10x10/0.5 both exist: SOT314-2 LQFP64 and SOT357-1 TQFP64), so height class is a pure thickness parameter (`body_thickness`), not a different outline.

**Note on the backlog name "QFP-32"/"TQFP-xx":** OHMNI uses the manufacturer-neutral name; the thickness class is a parameter. Defaults below follow the backlog name (TQFP for 32/44/64/100, LQFP for 144).

| foot angle | 0 deg | 0-7 deg (NXP theta), 0-13 deg (Microchip L1 foot angle) | MFR_DRAWING, M |

Lead exit height above PCB: z_exit = A1 + A2/2 (OHMNI assumption: sheets give no exit height; real parts vary). Foot underside z = 0, foot top z = c. Outer bend radii are LOD2 only (suggest inner R = c, outer R = 2c; common practice, not from a source).

Only D, E, e, A, A2 and HD are therefore trusted; HD cross-checks as D + 2.0 on every compact-style member. Lead width/thickness are capped at M/L (Section 17 item 7).

Validation: pitch x (n-1) must be < D with margin: 5.6<7, 8.0<10, 7.5<10, 12.0<14, 17.5<20, all OK, leaving 1.0-1.2 mm corner margin per end (symmetry: (D-span)/2 = 0.7, 1.0, 1.25, 1.0, 1.25).

### Pin-1 and numbering (Section 6)
Pin 1 = top-most lead on the LEFT (-X) side, numbering counter-clockwise from top: left side top-to-bottom (1..n), bottom side left-to-right (n+1..2n), right side bottom-to-top (2n+1..3n), top side right-to-left (3n+1..4n). Foot-contact center of lead i (i=0..n-1) on the left side: x = -(HD/2 - L/2), y = +(n-1)e/2 - i e.

### Pin-1 marking
Molded-in dimple (circle) on the top face near the pin-1 corner. Microchip drawing states only that the "Pin 1 visual index feature may vary but must be located within the hatched area" (area near pin-1 corner). OHMNI default: circular dimple, diameter 0.6/0.8/1.0/1.2 for D = 7/10/14/20, depth 0.05, center 1.0 mm inboard of both edges of the corner nearest pin 1 (top-left): UNCERTAIN, decal-class feature. Some vendors also bevel the pin-1 corner of the top face; optional LOD2 feature.

### Materials
Body MAT_EPOXY_BLACK (laser-mark patch lightens). Leads MAT_TIN_MATTE (matte tin or NiPdAu looks similar).

### Generator notes
Parameters: N, e, D, HD, A1, A2, b, c, L, foot_angle, dimple. Coupled: n=N/4, span=(n-1)e <= D - 1.0; lead tip span HD = D + 2*(overhang) with overhang = 1.0 (compact style); lead z_exit = A1 + A2/2; total seated height A1 + A2 + 0 must be <= A max (check: 0.10+1.00=1.10 <= 1.20 OK; 0.10+1.40=1.50 <= 1.60 OK).

## PACKAGE FAMILY: PKG-QFN

**Generator:** GEN-QFN. **Members:** QFN-16 (OHM-127), QFN-20 (128), QFN-24 (129), QFN-32 (130), QFN-48 (131). All class B. All members use a central exposed pad.

### Shared geometry
Square plastic body (molded epoxy), no leads: rectangular copper terminals lie flush with the underside and with the four side walls. Terminals are N/4 per side at pitch e, centered on each side. A square exposed die pad (EP, size Dh x Eh) sits at the center of the underside, coplanar with the terminals. The EP is separated from the nearest terminal ends by at least K (= 0.20 min, shown as "K" or "k" in the ADI, onsemi and Renesas sheets). Terminal outer face is flush with the body side wall (sawn-singulated style; no pullback). A3 = 0.20 REF is the lead-frame thickness shown in ADI, onsemi and Renesas drawings.

Body thickness / seated height A: NXP HVQFN family 0.85 nominal (0.80-1.00 max); Renesas TQFN 0.75 (0.70-0.80); onsemi QFN 0.80-1.00; NXP HUQFN24 ("ultra thin") 0.65. OHMNI default 0.85. Standoff A1: 0.00-0.05 (nominal 0.02): the body underside sits ~0.02 above the terminal underside; terminals at Z=0.

JEDEC outline: MO-220 is cited on the NXP SOT758-1, SOT617-5, SOT616-3, SOT619-13, SOT662-1 sheets, the Renesas TQFN sheet ("MO-220WGGD-1 Issue I") and the ADI UF20 drawing ("MO-220 VARIATION (WGGD-1) - TO BE APPROVED"). The MO-220 text itself was NOT opened, so variant letters are cited only as printed there. Pin-1 identification in the ADI drawing: notch "R = 0.20 TYP or 0.35 x 45 chamfer" at the pin-1 corner of the exposed pad region (reading from the extracted text; the location detail is from the drawing callout).

RESEARCH_REQUIRED for any 0.4 mm quad QFN; the generator accepts e = 0.4 with b ~0.20 and a flagged status.

Validation: row = (n-1)e = NXP e1/e2 callouts for 16/24/48 (1.5, 2.5, 5.5): matches. Inner gap between terminal inner end (D/2 - L) and EP edge (Dh/2): 16: 1.10-0.80=0.30; 20: 1.60-1.35=0.25; 24: 1.60-1.225=0.375; 32: 2.10-1.65=0.45; 48: 3.10-2.75=0.35: all >= K 0.20. Terminal row + terminal width within body: row + b < D (1.75<3 etc.).

### Pin numbering (Section 6)
Pin 1 at the top-most terminal on the left side, CCW from top view (left side top-to-bottom, bottom side left-to-right, right side bottom-to-top, top side right-to-left). The exposed pad is NOT numbered (OHMNI nets it as the "EP"/pin N+1 in the footprint, not modeled).

### Appearance and markings
Body MAT_EPOXY_BLACK. Terminals and EP MAT_TIN_MATTE (bright tin plating is common; sawn terminal side faces expose bare copper, MAT_COPPER, at LOD2). Pin-1 marker: molded or printed dot/dimple at the top-left corner, optional chamfered/notched pad corner on the EP and a chamfered terminal-row start (see ADI note above). Top marking is a laser decal.

### Optional wettable flank (LOD2 parameter `wettable_flank`)
TI RUG0010A (X2QFN, 10-pin): "Minimum 0.1 mm solder wetting on pin side wall. Available for wettable flank version only", with a "(0.127) TYP" callout on the flank detail. OHMNI models a flank as a stepped recess cut in the lower outer edge of each terminal: depth 0.127 (UNCERTAIN, meaning of the callout is inferred), height 0.10. Default off (no side-wettable on the backlog parts).

### Generator notes
Parameters: N (multiple of 4), e, D, L, b, A, A1, Dh, K. Coupled: n=N/4; (n-1)e + b <= D - 0.4 (corner margin); D/2 - L - Dh/2 >= K. Terminal pad ends are rectangles with sharp corners (NXP shows "rounded/half-etched" none).

## PACKAGE FAMILY: PKG-DFN

**Generator:** GEN-QFN (two-sided mode). **Members:** DFN-6 (OHM-132, class B), DFN-8 (133, class B), WSON-8 (134, class C parameter variant: finer pitch, different EP).

### Naming (important)
DFN (dual flat no-lead), SON/VSON/WSON/HVSON are different NAMES for the same construction: molded body, terminals in two opposite rows, flush with the underside and with the side walls, plus (usually) a central exposed pad. Evidence seen in opened documents: onsemi calls the 3x3, 0.65 pitch 8-terminal part "DFN8" (CASE 506BW); NXP calls the 3.3x3.3 sibling "DFN3333-8" with the title "thermal enhanced very thin small outline package; no leads"; TI labels the 2x2, 0.5 pitch 8-pin part "WSON-8" (drawing DSG0008A). No opened document defines WSON or states that WSON and DFN are identical, so "WSON = DFN naming variant" is OHMNI's inference (outline family is the same; thickness class may differ). `WSON` therefore reuses the DFN generator; entry OHM-134 differs only by body 2x2, pitch 0.5 and its own EP.

### Shared geometry
Rectangular terminals on the two long sides, parallel to Y (Section 6 dual-row rule: rows parallel to Y, row spacing along X). Terminals' outer faces flush with the body walls (K gap to EP at least 0.20 as in onsemi DFN8 `K` >= 0.20). Exposed pad: rectangle, long axis along the pin-row direction (Y). Seated height A 0.80-1.00 (onsemi), 0.65 (NXP DFN2020MD-6), 0.80 max (TI DSG0008A). A1 0-0.05. Lead-frame thickness 0.20 (A3 0.20 REF convention from the QFN sheets; not explicitly shown for DFN, DERIVED).

Body MAT_EPOXY_BLACK; terminals and EP MAT_TIN_MATTE. Pin-1: molded dimple or printed dot at the top-left; chamfered EP corner optional. Pin-1 marking details were not legible in any opened DFN sheet: UNCERTAIN, decal-class.

## PACKAGE FAMILY: PKG-PLCC

**Generator:** GEN-PLCC. **Member:** PLCC-28 (OHM-135, class A). Not to be confused with PKG-PLCC_LED (G-LED owner, a different package).

### Shared geometry
Square plastic body with J-leads on all four sides, 7 leads per side, 1.27 mm (0.050 in) pitch. Each lead exits the side wall near mid-height, drops down the wall, and curls under the body edge in a J, so the contact apex is below and slightly inboard of the body edge. Body has a larger, plain top face and a stepped/beveled skirt; the top-left (pin-1) region has a chamfered corner or index feature, depending on the maker.

| Dimension (NXP SOT261-2, mm; extraction-scrambled columns noted) | Value |
|---|---|
| Body D = E | 11.48 nominal (11.43-11.58) |
| Lead-tip span HD = HE | 12.32-12.57 (12.45 nominal) |
| Seated height A | 4.19-4.57 (4.57 max) |
| Body-underside standoff | ADI MO-047-AB drawing: 0.64-1.14 (0.025-0.045 in); NXP SOT261-2 extraction 0.02-0.12 (implausible), SOT261-3 A1 0.13 min; OHMNI default 0.64, L-M |
| Lead width bp | 0.66-0.81 (as extracted) |
| Lead pitch e | 1.27 |
| Row: (n-1) x e | 6 x 1.27 = 7.62 |

The extraction listed other values (b1 0.456-0.495, ZD 9.91-10.92, kD/kE not defined, w 2.16, v 0.026-0.048) whose headings do not match inch-converted JEDEC-style values; only D, HD, A, e and bp are used. All of these remain M at best.

Standards seen: NXP SOT261-2 cites JEDEC MS-018, IEC 112E08, JEITA EDR-7319 (designations as printed; MS-018 text NOT opened).

### OHMNI defaults (PLCC-28)
- Body 11.48 x 11.48. Body top at Z = A = 4.57 (NXP seated height max; leads curl below the body to reach Z = 0). Body underside at Z = 0.64 (ADI MO-047-AB standoff low end, see table), so body slab spans Z 0.64 to 4.57 (thickness 3.93).
- J-lead: width 0.45 (0.33-0.53 per NXP SOT261-3 as extracted), thickness 0.20 (UNCERTAIN), exits side wall at Z = 2.4, drops to lower apex, curls inward under the body.
- Contact apex (pad contact center) radial position DERIVED: r = HD/2 - 0.45 = 5.78 (the apex sits about one bend radius inboard of the lead-tip span); L confidence.

### Numbering and pin 1
Pin 1 is the CENTER lead (itwissen.info: mark in the middle of one side, counterclockwise from above; M-L) of the top side, numbering counter-clockwise from top view (pins 2-4 run LEFT along the top side, then left side top-to-bottom 5-11, bottom side left-to-right 12-18, right side bottom-to-top 19-25, top side right-to-left 26-28). This differs from Section 6's "top-left" quad rule; Section 6 says to follow the standard and record the delta, but since the standard text was not opened, the generator exposes `pin1_mode` = `center_top` (default, common practice) | `section6_topleft`. YAML pin1_xy is given for the default mode. Still wanted: a legible vendor numbering diagram (NXP, ADI and Renesas sheets show only 'pin 1 identifier' in extraction).

Pin-1 index: a large chamfered/beveled top corner (45 degrees, ~1.0 mm legs) on the top-left corner nearest pin 1 plus a molded dimple; both are common practice, not extracted from a drawing. UNCERTAIN.

### Materials
Body MAT_PLASTIC_BLACK would also work, but use MAT_EPOXY_BLACK (molded IC body). Leads MAT_TIN_MATTE.

## PACKAGE FAMILY: PKG-BGA

**Generator:** GEN-BGA. **Members:** BGA-64 (OHM-136), BGA-100 (137), BGA-256 (138). All class B. Ball maps are full rectangular arrays (no depopulated centers) in the opened sources.

### Shared geometry
Square or rectangular package body (a substrate with an over-molded or exposed top) with an N x N area array of solder balls on the underside. Balls are collapsed (flattened) after reflow: the PCB-contact (collapsed) ball stand-off A1 is less than the as-supplied ball diameter b. Model each ball as a sphere of diameter b truncated by two planes: flat at Z=0 (PCB side; solder fillet not modeled) and flat at Z = A1 (substrate side). Body underside at Z = A1. Body top at Z = A1 + A2, where A2 is body thickness; overall seated height A (max) bounds it (A1 + A2 <= A max).

Ball (i, j): i = row 0..N-1 top to bottom, j = column 0..N-1 left to right, center x = (j - (N-1)/2) * e, y = ((N-1)/2 - i) * e. Ball A1 = (row 0, col 0) = top-left corner (Section 6; OHMNI top view). Checked against NXP e1/e2 callouts: (N-1)e = e1 = e2 (5.6 for 8 balls at 0.8; 7.2 for 10 at 0.8).

Pin-1 index: A1 corner. NXP says only "A1 index area as shown in the outline drawing" (location not legible). OHMNI default: an inked dot or small corner chamfer on the top face at the top-left corner, plus the missing/larger A1 index mark; decal-class.

Row naming (second pass, M): the skip rule is confirmed by observation in an opened drawing. Renesas V356.27x27B (356-ball PBGA, 20 x 20 matrix, "conforms to JEDEC MS-034/A variation BAL-2") prints its row letters, in order, as A B C D E F G H J K L M N P R T U V W Y (20 rows); I, O, Q, S, X, Z are absent. The ADI 625-ball PBGA drawing (B-625, "complies with JEDEC MS-034") shows rows A..Y then AA..AE: 20 single letters + 5 = 25 rows, consistent with the same skip set; the ADI 484-ball drawing (rows A..Y, AA, AB = 22 rows) also fits. ADI uModule BGA144 drawing 05-08-1551 states "BALL DESIGNATION PER JESD MS-028 AND JEP95" (the JEP95 text itself NOT opened, so the rule is cited as observed practice in JEDEC-conformant drawings, not as quoted standard text). Generator parameter `row_letters` default "ABCDEFGHJKLMNPRTUVWY" (then AA, AB, ...). Coordinates do not depend on letters. For the sizes here: BGA-64 rows A-H, BGA-100 rows A-H,J,K ("ABCDEFGHJK"), BGA-256 rows A-H,J-N,P,R,T ("ABCDEFGHJKLMNPRT", 16 letters). The A1 corner location is stated only as "Pin A1 is marked on the top and bottom sides adjacent to A1" (Renesas V100.11x11, V256.17x17) and "A1 index ... must be located within the zone indicated ... mold or marked feature" (ADI 05-08-1551); which corner A1 occupies in OHMNI's top view remains the Section 6 convention (top-left), NOT verified from an opened vendor statement; datasheet bottom-view maps are mirror images of the top view.

JEDEC outlines: NXP SOT740-2 cites "JEDEC MO-192" (extracted); the NXP SOT926-1 and SOT534-1 sheets give no usable JEDEC number (SOT926-1 lists "TFBGA100" as JEDEC code, not a standard). MO-205 / MO-216 were NOT seen: not cited.

Collapsed standoff 0.35 is DERIVED (ball 0.40, <= 0.50 headroom). The extracted SOT926-1 text says "10x10 grid with corner balls removed", but 100 balls = 10x10 full, and e1 = e2 = 7.2 = 9 x 0.8 describes a full 10-ball row; OHMNI uses a FULL array.

Depopulated/ perimeter-only maps: none in opened sources. Generator supports `depopulate: none | center_NxN | perimeter_rows` for user parts. Defaults: none.

### Materials
Body top MAT_EPOXY_BLACK (over-mold) with MAT_PLASTIC_BLACK acceptable; underside substrate: propose MAT_BGA_SUBSTRATE (#2F4F3A, rough 0.5, dark green solder mask). Balls MAT_SOLDER_BALL.

### Generator notes
Parameters: N_x, N_y, e, D, E, A1, A2, b, depopulate set, corner chamfer. Coupled: (N-1)e + b <= D - 0.4; A1 + A2 <= A max. Balls: 12-16 segments at LOD1; instance one ball mesh for all positions.

## PACKAGE FAMILY: PKG-WLCSP

**Generator:** GEN-BGA (WLCSP mode). **Members:** WLCSP-9 (OHM-139), WLCSP-16 (140). Class B.

### Shared geometry
A bare silicon die (rectangular, may be non-square) with a redistribution layer, a passivation/back-side coating and a solder-bump array on the active face. There is no mold, substrate, leadframe or underfill. Body = die: thickness A2 (die plus back coat), bumps below. WLCSP body is usually dark gray to black (back-side laminate) with a laser-marked top; edges are sawn silicon (lighter gray, thin).

Bump geometry: sphere-like bumps truncated at the PCB plane (collapsed standoff A - A2). Ball (i, j) positions as in PKG-BGA with N x N array centered on the die unless the datasheet says otherwise (opened NXP/Renesas sheets do not give the array offset: assumed centered; RESEARCH_REQUIRED for off-center arrays).

Pin-1: ball A1 at the top-left in the OHMNI top view (Section 6). Back side typically marked with a dot or chamfered/notched corner in line with A1: UNCERTAIN, decal-class.

### Member table
| Member | OHM | Source | die D x E | A2 (die + back coat) | A seated height | collapsed standoff A-A2 | ball diameter b | e | array | span |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

# [OHM-122] QFP-32
## Identity
- Canonical name: QFP-32 (TQFP thickness class, 7 x 7 mm body, 0.8 mm pitch, 32 leads)

- Mounting: SMD
- Aliases / names: TQFP-32, LQFP-32 (7x7 variant), PT package (Microchip/Atmel legacy code AUT), QFP32
- Common variants: other thickness class at same outline (see PKG-QFP); exposed-pad "H" variants (NXP HTQFP/HLQFP, e.g. SOT638-6, SOT855-1, SOT1510-4) add a top or bottom heat slug (not modeled here)
- Class B, priority P1, complexity 3

## Physical Dimensions
Member row (from PKG-QFP, restated; mm):
- Body: 7 x 7; body thickness A2 = 1; seated height A max = 1.2; standoff A1 = 0.1 (default)
- Lead pitch e = 0.8; leads per side n = 8; lead row length (n-1)e = 5.6
- Lead-tip span HD = 9; lead overhang per side = 1
- Lead: width b = 0.35; thickness c = 0.15; foot length L = 0.6; foot angle 0 deg
- Overall footprint of leads (tip to tip) = 9 x 9
Basis/confidence: D, e, A2, A max, HD from Microchip C04-074-PT Rev D (32-lead TQFP 7x7x1.0) (MFR_DRAWING, M-H). b and c: see PKG-QFP lead table (M/L). A1: DERIVED default 0.10 (range 0-0.2). Ambiguity: The backlog default says 'LQFP/TQFP, 7x7 0.8 pitch'. The only opened 7x7 / 0.8 / 32-lead drawing is Microchip's TQFP (body 1.0). NXP SOT401-1 (LQFP32) is 5x5x1.4 per its title (pitch not extracted) and is NOT this part. A 7x7x1.4 LQFP32 at 0.8 pitch is plausible but no opened drawing shows it: set body_thickness=1.4 for that variant (RESEARCH_REQUIRED).

## Geometry
Primary: rectangular slab 7 x 7 x 1 (Z from 0.1 to 1.1). Secondary: 32 gull-wing leads, 8 per side. Each lead is a sheet of width 0.35 and thickness 0.15: it exits the body side wall at Z = 0.6 (mid-thickness, OHMNI assumption), runs horizontally outward, drops with a shoulder to the board plane, then runs outward as a flat foot of length 0.6 ending at the tip span 9. Foot underside at Z = 0. Body top face has a pin-1 dimple. Side walls are vertical at LOD0-1; mold draft (about 5-10 deg is common practice, not sourced) only at LOD2. Corners of the body are square (optionally 0.2 mm edge break at LOD2).

## Leads / Pins / Terminals
- Count 32; type gull-wing; pitch 0.8; width 0.35; thickness 0.15; foot length 0.6; material MAT_TIN_MATTE
- Position (foot contact center, Section 17.1): left side x = -4.2, y from +2.8 (pin 1) stepping -0.8 to -2.8; right side x = +4.2; top/bottom sides y = +/-4.2, x from -2.8 to +2.8
- Numbering: counter-clockwise from top view, pin 1 = top-most lead on the left side; pins 1..8 down the left side, 9..16 bottom (left to right), 17..24 right side (bottom to top), 25..32 top side (right to left)
- Bends: inner bend radius c (0.15) at both bends, LOD2 only. PCB penetration none.

## PCB Interface
SMD pads under each foot. FCO origin (Section 4) = center of lead-pad pattern = body center; body_offset (0, 0). Pin 1 contact center at (-4.2, 2.8). Body underside 0.1 above the board; foot undersides at Z=0. No thermal pad. Standoff for the model = A1 = 0.1.

## Materials
Body MAT_EPOXY_BLACK (laser-mark patch #6E6E70 permitted by Section 7); leads MAT_TIN_MATTE. No new tokens.

## Appearance
Matte black body, matte-silver leads. Top: laser marking text (decal), pin-1 dimple circle diameter 0.6 mm (UNCERTAIN). Geometry vs decal: dimple geometry optional at LOD0, a decal at LOD1+. Manufacturer variation: marking position, ejector-pin marks on the bottom, dimple size.

## Orientation Markings
Pin 1: molded dimple near the top-left corner of the top face (corner nearest the pin-1 lead, i.e. the -X,+Y corner). Some parts add a chamfered/bevelled corner or a second marked 'pin-1 side' stripe; Microchip's drawing only requires the index be inside a hatched area near the pin-1 corner.

## Recognition Features
1. Square body with leads on all four sides, correct lead count per side (8) and pitch 0.8.
2. Gull-wing lead profile: shoulder then flat foot, with tip span 9 and visible overhang 1.
3. Slim body thickness (1 mm class TQFP).
4. Pin-1 dimple at the top-left corner.
5. Matte silver leads against black body.

## Parametric Variants
Safe parameters: thickness class (A2 1.0 / 1.4, A max 1.2 / 1.6), lead width, foot length, dimple size, standoff. Coupled: n = N/4; (n-1)e <= D - 1.0; lead-tip span HD = D + 2*overhang (compact style overhang 1.0); z_exit = A1 + A2/2; A1 + A2 <= A max. Changing e requires changing b (b ~ 0.45 e for 0.5 pitch; 0.44 e for 0.8).

## Recommended Base Geometry
Box (body), swept thin-rectangle polyline per lead (exit, shoulder, foot) instanced along the four sides with array transform; small cylinder cut for the dimple.

## Modeling Procedure
1. Create body box 7 x 7 x 1 centered at XY origin, bottom at Z = 0.1.
2. Build one lead profile in the XZ plane: start at body wall (x = 3.5, z = 0.6), horizontal run, shoulder to z = 0.15/2 center line, foot out to x = 4.5; extrude width 0.35 along Y.
3. Instance 8 leads along the right side at pitch 0.8, centered; rotate the set by 90, 180, 270 deg for the other sides.
4. Cut pin-1 dimple (dia 0.6, depth 0.05) near the (-X,+Y) corner.
5. Assign materials; apply marking decal.

## LOD Strategy
- LOD0: body box plus four lead strips (one extruded bar per side with the foot profile, no individual leads); about 60 triangles.
- LOD1: individual 32 leads (box segments for exit, shoulder, foot), dimple, standoff; roughly 990 triangles.
- LOD2: add lead bend radii, body mold draft, edge breaks, ejector marks, lead end chamfers.

## Simplification Rules
May omit: bend radii, draft, ejector marks, lead end bevels, dimple at LOD0. Never omit: correct lead count/pitch per side, tip span, body size and thickness, pin-1 side (marker or at least the pin-1 coordinate), lead standoff so feet touch Z = 0.

# [OHM-127] QFN-16
## Identity
- Canonical name: QFN-16 (3 x 3 mm body, 0.5 mm pitch, 16 terminals + exposed pad)
- ID: OHM-127; slug `qfn_16`; Category: ic; Subcategory: quad flat no-lead
- Physical package: PKG-QFN member `QFN-16`; generator GEN-QFN; Mounting: SMD
- Aliases: QFN16, VQFN-16, HVQFN16 (NXP name), WQFN/TQFN/UQFN variants (thickness class), MLF/MLP/LFCSP (vendor trade names, not opened)
- Common variants: 0.4/0.65 pitch, ultra-thin 0.65 body, wettable-flank; Also common: 4x4 mm 0.65 pitch 16-terminal bodies; not opened (RESEARCH_REQUIRED). Backlog request names 3x3 and 4x4 for 16: only 3x3 at 0.5 pitch is sourced.
- Class B, priority P1, complexity 3

## Physical Dimensions
- Body 3 x 3 (+/-0.1), seated height A = 0.85 (max 1.00 NXP; Renesas variants 0.75), standoff A1 = 0.02 (0-0.05)
- Terminals: 16 total, 4 per side, pitch 0.5, width 0.25 (0.18-0.30), length L = 0.4 (family range 0.30-0.50), thickness 0.20 (A3 REF)
- Exposed pad: 1.6 x 1.6 (range seen: 1.45-1.75 (NXP SOT758-1)); gap to terminal inner end = 0.300 (>= K 0.20)
- Terminal row length (n-1) x e = 1.5
Basis: NXP SOT758-1 HVQFN16 (3x3x0.85, MO-220) (MFR_DRAWING, M-H); terminal b/L family consensus (M); EP size is product-specific (M/L).

## Geometry
Body slab 3 x 3 x (0.83) with bottom at Z = 0.02 and top at Z = 0.85. Underside: 4 rectangular terminals (0.25 x 0.4) per side, outer faces flush with the body side wall and bottoms at Z = 0; terminal height 0.20 (visible on the side wall as a copper/tin strip). Central exposed pad 1.6 square at Z = 0 (0.0-0.05 proud/flush). Pin-1 corner: dimple on the top face; the exposed pad may carry a chamfered corner toward pin 1 (ADI UF20 callout R 0.20 or 0.35 x 45; UNCERTAIN as to which corner). Body edges square; no leads, no bends.

## Leads / Pins / Terminals
- 16 flat pads, pitch 0.5, 0.25 wide, 0.4 long (radially), thickness 0.20; material MAT_TIN_MATTE (plating on bottom, bare copper on the sawn edge at LOD2); no PCB penetration
- Positions (terminal underside center): left side x = -1.3, y = +0.75 .. -0.75 step -0.5; bottom y = -1.3, x = -0.75 .. +0.75; right x = +1.3, y = -0.75 .. +0.75; top y = +1.3, x = +0.75 .. -0.75
- Numbering: ccw; pin 1 = top-most terminal on the left side (-1.3, 0.75); 1..4 left (down), 5..8 bottom (left to right), 9..12 right (up), 13..16 top (right to left); exposed pad un-numbered (netted as N+1 in footprint)

## PCB Interface
SMD lands under each terminal plus a central thermal land. FCO origin = body center (pad pattern bounding box is symmetric). Body offset (0,0). Standoff of body bottom 0.02; terminal/EP undersides at Z = 0. thermal_pad = true (1.6 x 1.6).

## Materials
Body MAT_EPOXY_BLACK; terminals and EP MAT_TIN_MATTE (MAT_COPPER for side edges at LOD2). No new tokens.

## Appearance
Black matte top face with laser mark (decal) and pin-1 dot. Bottom: silver terminals around a larger silver square EP, black mold compound between. Manufacturer variation: EP size and shape (some have EP corner chamfers or tie bars), marking, dot vs. dimple vs. corner notch.

## Orientation Markings
Pin 1 at the top-left corner: dimple/dot on the top face near the corner of terminal 1; terminal 1 sometimes slightly longer or the corner chamfered (ADI UF20: notch R 0.20 or 0.35 x 45 chamfer). Default OHMNI: dimple dia 0.4 (scaled with body) 0.4 in from the top-left corner.

## Recognition Features
1. Square thin body with 4 flush rectangular terminals per side at 0.5 pitch.
2. Large square exposed pad on the underside centered, with a clear gap to the terminals.
3. No visible leads from the top (terminals visible only at the very edge and underside).
4. Pin-1 dimple at top-left.
5. Thin profile (0.85 mm).

## Parametric Variants
Safe: body size, N, pitch (0.4/0.5/0.65), EP size, terminal b/L, A (0.65 / 0.75 / 0.85 / 1.0), wettable_flank on/off. Coupled: n = N/4; (n-1)e + b <= D - 0.4; D/2 - L - Dh/2 >= 0.20; Dh <= D - 2L - 0.4.

## Recommended Base Geometry
Box (body), box instances for terminals (array along four sides), box for EP, optional cylinder cut for the dimple.

## Modeling Procedure
1. Body box 3 x 3, Z 0.02 to 0.85.
2. EP: box 1.6 x 1.6, Z 0 to 0.05, centered.
3. One terminal box 0.4 (radial) x 0.25 x 0.20, bottom at Z = 0, outer face at x = -1.5; instance 4 along Y at pitch 0.5 centered, so first center is y = +0.75.
4. Rotate instanced set 90/180/270 deg for the other sides.
5. Cut pin-1 dimple on the top face; apply materials/decals.

## LOD Strategy
- LOD0: body box + EP + four terminal strips (merged); under 70 triangles.
- LOD1: all 16 terminals individually, EP, dimple (about 252 triangles).
- LOD2: add copper side-edge strips, optional wettable-flank steps, EP corner chamfer, terminal tie-bar stubs.

## Simplification Rules
May omit: dimple, side-edge copper, flank steps, EP corner chamfer. Never omit: terminal count per side, pitch, EP presence and size, terminals flush to the body edge, body size, pin-1 position.

# [OHM-135] PLCC-28
## Identity
- Canonical name: PLCC-28 (plastic leaded chip carrier, 28 J-leads, 1.27 mm pitch, 11.5 mm class body)
- ID: OHM-135; slug `plcc_28`; Category: ic; Subcategory: leaded chip carrier (J-lead)
- Physical package: PKG-PLCC; generator GEN-PLCC; Mounting: SMD (also socketable)
- Aliases: PLCC28, PLCC-28, J-lead chip carrier, 28-lead PLCC. NOT the PLCC LED package (PKG-PLCC_LED).
- Common variants: 20/32/44/52/68/84 pins (same 1.27 pitch), square only for 28
- Class A, priority P3, complexity 3

## Physical Dimensions
- Body D = E = 11.48 (11.43-11.58); lead-tip span HD = HE = 12.45 (12.32-12.57); seated height A = 4.57 (4.19-4.57 max)
- Pitch 1.27; leads per side 7; row length 7.62
- Body underside standoff = 0.64 (range 0.64-1.14, ADI PLCC 28 drawing labelled MO-047-AB; first-pass 0.51 from NXP SOT261-2 extraction retained as the low end; NXP SOT261-3 extraction shows A1 0.13 min, a different definition; M-L)
- J-lead width 0.45 (range 0.33-0.53: NXP SOT261-3 extraction b1 0.33 / bp 0.53 as printed; the 0.66-0.81 and 1.07-1.22 values seen in other extractions are the wider shoulder/neck width, not the foot width), thickness 0.20 (UNCERTAIN, not on any sheet)
Basis: NXP SOT261-2 (S2): D, HD, A, e (M); ADI p_28 MO-047-AB drawing: D 11.43-11.58, HD (their D1) 12.32-12.57, A 4.19-4.57 as listed, pitch 1.27: the same body/tip span as NXP (second source, H for D/HD). Lead details L-M.

## Geometry
Primary: square body 11.48 x 11.48, top Z = 4.57, bottom Z = 0.64. The upper body is vertical-walled; the lower skirt may step in slightly (common practice, not sourced). Secondary: 28 J-leads, 7 per side. Each lead leaves the side wall at Z about 2.4, runs out 0.4-0.5 mm (to the tip span, HD/2 = 6.225), turns down, and curls inward under the body in a J with its lowest point (contact apex) near r = 5.78 and Z = 0. The J curl ends under the body bottom face. Pin-1 corner: bevelled (45 deg, 1.0 x 1.0) top-left corner of the top face, plus a molded dimple (both common practice, UNCERTAIN).

## Leads / Pins / Terminals
- 28 J-leads, width 0.45, thickness 0.20, pitch 1.27, material MAT_TIN_MATTE
- Contact apex centers: left side x = -5.775, y from +3.81 to -3.81; right x = +5.775; top/bottom y = +/-5.775
- Numbering (default mode `center_top`; itwissen.info, an engineering reference, states pin 1 is 'the mark in the middle of one side' and numbering is counterclockwise seen from above; no opened vendor drawing's numbering diagram was legible; M-L): pin 1 = center lead of the top side at (0, +5.775); counter-clockwise from top: pins 2-4 on the top side moving left (x = -1.27, -2.54, -3.81), 5-11 left side top to bottom, 12-18 bottom left to right, 19-25 right side bottom to top, 26-28 top side right to left (x = +3.81, +2.54, +1.27). Alternative mode `section6_topleft`: pin 1 = top lead on the left side (-5.775, +3.81), 7 per side CCW. This deviates from Section 6 (top-left) by default; the delta is recorded here and the mode is a parameter. Still wanted: confirmation from a legible vendor numbering diagram (non-blocking).
- PCB penetration none.

## PCB Interface
SMD J-lead lands. FCO origin = body center. Body offset (0,0). Contact apex Z = 0, body bottom 0.64 above the board. No thermal pad. Pin 1 at (0, 5.775) in default mode.

## Materials
Body MAT_EPOXY_BLACK; leads MAT_TIN_MATTE. No new tokens.

## Appearance
Large black square body, matte-silver J-leads curled under; top-face laser marking; beveled pin-1 corner and dimple. Variation: bevel size, marking, body skirt step.

## Orientation Markings
Pin 1: top-center lead (default mode) with the beveled corner and dimple on the top face immediately next to it (UNCERTAIN, common practice). The bevel corner should sit at the top-left corner of the top face.

## Recognition Features
1. Tall square body (4.57 mm) with J-leads tucked under, no foot protruding outward.
2. 7 leads per side at 1.27 pitch.
3. Beveled pin-1 corner / dimple.
4. 11.5 mm class body.

## Parametric Variants
Safe: lead count (20/28/44/68/84 by changing n; body D = n*1.27 + 2.6 approx., not sourced), lead width, standoff, bevel size. Coupled: HD = D + 0.97 (SOT261-2: 12.45 - 11.48); span (n-1)e <= D - 2.0.

## Recommended Base Geometry
Box (body) with a chamfered corner cut; swept J-profile (rectangular section) instanced along four sides; cylinder cut for the dimple.

## Modeling Procedure
1. Body box 11.48 x 11.48, Z 0.64..4.57; chamfer the top-left vertical edge 1.0 and cut dimple.
2. J-lead profile in XZ: exit wall x = 5.74 at Z 2.4, out to x = 6.225, down, curl radius about 0.4 inward to apex x = 5.78 Z = 0, continue to x = 5.2 under the body at Z = 0.2; extrude 0.45 in Y.
3. Instance 7 leads at pitch 1.27 per side; rotate sides by 90 deg.
4. Apply numbering mode; materials; decal.

## LOD Strategy
- LOD0: body box + four lead strips; < 80 triangles.
- LOD1: 28 individual J-leads, bevel, dimple.
- LOD2: curl radii, skirt step, mold draft, lead tip bevels.

## Simplification Rules
May omit: skirt step, draft, radii. Never omit: J-lead curl under body (not gull-wing), 7 leads/side, body height, pin-1 corner/bevel and pin-1 location.

Safe: N_x, N_y, pitch, die size, thickness, bump diameter, array offset. Coupled: (N-1)e + b <= min(Dx,Dy) - 0.1; bump height <= b; bump dia <= 0.65 e.

## Recommended Base Geometry
Box (die), instanced truncated spheres in a grid, small disc for A1 mark.

## Modeling Procedure
1. Die box 2.05 x 2.05, Z 0.230..0.555.
2. Bump mesh dia 0.23 truncated at Z=0 and Z=0.230.
3. Grid 4 x 4 at pitch 0.5, first center (-0.75, 0.75).
4. A1 mark, materials.

## LOD Strategy
- LOD0: box + hex-prism bumps.
- LOD1: round bumps (8-12 segments), A1 mark.
- LOD2: smoother bumps, chamfered die edges, RDL/passivation detail is NOT modeled.

## Simplification Rules
May omit: marking, die edge chamfer. Never omit: bump grid size/pitch, bump standoff, die proportions, A1 corner.

# G10: Display modules and frequency-control parts

Group G10 covers OHM-087..092 (displays) and OHM-141..149 (frequency control). Evidence level: all sources were read through a text-extraction fetch tool. Most Kingbright and Abracon package drawings did NOT survive extraction (only overall size lines did), so many pad/pin sizes are RESEARCH_REQUIRED and carry OHMNI visual defaults flagged DERIVED/UNCERTAIN. No WebSearch budget remained for the second half of the session, so the SAW filter, LED matrix and HC-49/U outlines could not be sourced from opened documents (see per-entry notes).

Orientation note for dual-row displays: rows parallel to Y, row spacing along X (Section 6 of 00_architecture). A datasheet-upright digit (pin 1 bottom-left, pins numbered counter-clockwise, bottom row first) is rotated 90 degrees clockwise to get this layout, so at rotation 0 the digit's UP direction is +X and the decimal point lies on the -X/-Y corner side of the digit. Row spacing is therefore measured along the digit height axis.

Proposed new material tokens (coordinator to merge): MAT_LED_FACE_GRAY (#6B6B6B, rough 0.6, metallic 0), MAT_LED_FACE_BLACK (#1A1A1C, 0.55, 0), MAT_LED_SEGMENT_WHITE (#EDEDE8, rough 0.4, translucent alpha 0.85, emissive off), MAT_LCD_POLARIZER_GRAY (#7F8C7C, rough 0.3, 0), MAT_OLED_PANEL_BLACK (#08080A, rough 0.15, 0), MAT_CERAMIC_PKG_TAN (#C9C0A8, rough 0.6, 0), MAT_RESONATOR_COAT_BLUE (#5F86B4, rough 0.5, 0).

## PACKAGE FAMILY: PKG-7SEG

**Generator:** GEN-7SEG. Through-hole seven-segment LED display, DIP-like: a rectangular plastic housing (face plate on top, gray or black), one or more digits each with 7 bar segments plus a decimal point (DP), two parallel rows of 2.54 mm (0.100 in) pitch round/square pins at row spacing 7.62 mm (0.300 in, small digits) or 15.24 mm (0.600 in, 0.56 in class).

**Shared geometry.** Housing is a box (X = along the digit-height axis, Y = along the digit row axis, Z = height), top face flat with a recessed/inset face plate carrying the digit windows. Digits are upright (not italic) by default (slant parameter 0; actual slant per Kingbright not verified). Each digit = 7 bars (a,b,c,d,e,f,g) in a "figure-8" layout plus a round DP at the lower right of the digit (right-hand DP; the Kingbright SC56/DC56/SC39 selection tables state right-hand DP). Pins exit the bottom face in two rows parallel to Y. Pin centering: the pin pattern is centered on the body in both axes (confirmed only by arithmetic consistency, drawings not legible).

**Generator notes.** Parameters: digits (1, 2, 4), digit_height class (0.28 / 0.36 / 0.39 / 0.56 in), face_color (gray | black), body_x/y/z, row_spacing, pin_count, pin_pitch (2.54), pins_per_row = pin_count/2, DP on/off. Digit window sizes are derived from digit_height h: digit box width = 0.62 h, bar stroke = 0.14 h, DP diameter = 0.15 h, gap between bars 0.03 h (all DERIVED/UNCERTAIN OHMNI visual defaults; Kingbright segment dimensions were not legible in extraction). For multi-digit parts digit-to-digit pitch = body_y / digits (DERIVED, UNCERTAIN). Pin numbering: pin 1 at (-X,+Y); pins 1..N/2 go down the -X row, N/2+1..N go up the +X row (dual-row rule). Pin cross-section default 0.5 x 0.25 mm flat (UNCERTAIN, RESEARCH_REQUIRED: not read from any drawing); tail bottom default -2.6 mm.

**Face colors.** Kingbright standard appearance in every datasheet opened: "STANDARD: GRAY FACE, WHITE SEGMENT" (SC56-11EWA, DC56-11EWA, SC39-11EWA, CC56-12EWA, CA56-12). Black-face variants exist in the market (the OHMNI brief asks for gray/black); the specific Kingbright suffix for black face was not verified.

**Generator:** GEN-7SEG (shared with PKG-7SEG). 8x8 dot-matrix LED display, through-hole DIP-like housing. STATUS: partial. No dimensioned drawing for an 8x8 matrix was legible/opened. What was established: Kingbright TC23-11 series is "58 mm (2.3 INCH) 8x8 DOT MATRIX DISPLAY" (alldatasheet.com search result page https://www.alldatasheet.com/view.jsp?Searchword=TC23-11EWA, listing only, drawing not opened); Kingbright TC12-11SRWA (1.2 in, 5x7, 3 mm dot, gray face white dot) and TC20-11SRWA (2.0 in, 5x7, 5 mm dot, gray face white dot) datasheets were opened (https://www.kingbrightusa.com/images/catalog/SPEC/TC12-11SRWA.pdf and .../TC20-11SRWA.pdf) but are 5x7, not 8x8, and had no legible package dimensions. The generic "1588BS style 32x32 mm, 24-pin, 2 rows" in the brief could not be tied to an opened datasheet (alldatasheet search for 1588BS gave unrelated results).

**Shared geometry.** Square housing with a flat face plate (gray or black) carrying an 8x8 grid of round (or square) dot windows with white diffusers; two rows of 12 pins at 2.54 mm pitch (24 pins), rows parallel to Y, row spacing along X.

**Generator:** GEN-MODULE (class D assembly). Character LCD module of the 16x2 (1602) HD44780-compatible type, 80.0 x 36.0 mm FR4 PCB, one single-row 16-pin 2.54 mm header, four 2.5 mm corner mounting holes with 5.0 mm pads, a glass LCD stack with a window, optionally a metal bezel, and an LED backlight (edge-lit or array).

**Sub-bodies:** (1) PCB 80.0 x 36.0 x t_pcb; (2) LCD glass + polarizers + backlight stack; (3) bezel/frame (metal, optional); (4) header: 16 pins, 1.0 mm plated holes, 1.8 mm pads at 2.54 mm pitch (total 38.1 mm); (5) 4 mounting holes 2.5 PTH with 5.0 pads at 75.0 x 31.0 mm centers.

Conflicts shown: max thickness 10.0 / 13.2 / 13.5 across variants (variant dependent, not an error). ## PACKAGE FAMILY: PKG-XTAL_HC49

**Generator:** GEN-XTAL. Through-hole metal can crystal, two wire leads, can long axis along X.

**Shared geometry.** A rounded-rectangle ("stadium") can: length (X) 10.8 (U) / 11.05 (S), width (Y) 4.65, with a flat bottom seal plate and a glass bead / solder seal at the bottom where two round leads exit 4.88 mm apart (gap-fill: 4.88 +/-0.2 now sourced). HC-49/U is the tall can; HC-49/S (also written HC-49/US) is the low-profile version with the same footprint. Pin-1 is arbitrary (crystal is not polarized); terminal 1 at -X.

The 11.05 x 4.65 values are from the OHMNI task brief and widely used KiCad/IEC style outlines; no opened document states them. ## PACKAGE FAMILY: PKG-XTAL_SMD

**Generator:** GEN-XTAL. Ceramic-package SMD quartz crystal: a rectangular ceramic base with a metal (kovar/nickel-plated) lid seam-welded on top, four castellated or wraparound metallized pads at the corners (4-pad) or two pads at the short ends (2-pad). Pin 1 marking: a chamfer or dot, and the lid print reading left-to-right. For 4-pad crystals the diagonal pads (1,3) are the crystal terminals; pads 2 and 4 are ground/NC (electrically ignorable; keep all four visible). A 2-pad variant (common in 3225 for some vendors) uses pads at the two short ends: model with the two pads full-width at the ends (OHMNI note; not sourced, UNCERTAIN).

**Pin 1 rule (gap-fill revised).** Manufacturers differ, so the family default is a per-manufacturer table and the architecture default (top-left) is adopted:

| Manufacturer / doc | Pin 1 location (top view, text readable) | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Abracon ABM8G (3225) | bottom-left ("Per the Top Marking from left to right, Pin 1 is always located on the bottom left"); chamfer note on pin 4 | opened, first pass |
| Abracon ABM10W / ABM11W / ABM12W | not fixed by the chamfer ("Chamfer could be located on pin #1, 2 or 4") | opened, first pass |
| NDK NX2016SA | top-left (extraction of the top-view land connection diagram) | https://www.mouser.com/datasheet/2/905/c_NX2016SA_2_e-1890600.pdf, S3 |
| NDK NX2520SA | upper left | NX2520SA sheet via https://www.promelec.ru/fs/sources/e4/1a/d8/bc/5ada22877a90c002b2b26516.pdf, S4 |
| Epson FA-238V / TSX-3225 | upper-left / top-left | Epson sheets hosted at wmsc.lcsc.com (Q22FA23V00418, X1E000021087700), S4 |
| Epson TG3225CEN (TCXO) | pin map shows "#1 #2" on one edge and "#4 #3" on the other (rows, corner of #1 not stated in text) | https://atta.szlcsc.com/upload/public/pdf/source/20210917/3B82CC32ED3EC7F2497BAE68AC283908.pdf, S4 |

Decision: OHMNI default is pin 1 at top-left (-X,+Y), numbering counter-clockwise from the top (1 TL, 2 BL, 3 BR, 4 TR), because three of four manufacturers that state it (NDK, Epson, plus the Addendum 17.2 default) agree. Abracon's bottom-left rule is recorded as the variant `pin1_corner = BL` (mirror the pad numbering: 1 BL, 2 BR, 3 TR, 4 TL). First-pass entries used the Abracon rule; this is a change of default, not a contradiction of the datasheets. Counter-clockwise direction itself is inferred (NDK and Epson texts say pins 1 and 3 are the crystal terminals and 2 and 4 are tied to the lid/GND, which is symmetric). Pads 1/3 are the crystal terminals, 2/4 ground.

# [OHM-087] Single 7-segment display
## Identity
- Canonical name: Single 7-segment display; ID OHM-087; slug seg7_single
- Category: optoelectronic / display; Subcategory: seven-segment LED display
- Physical package: PKG-7SEG member 7SEG.056x1 (family DIP-like display, 10 pins)
- Mounting: through-hole. Aliases: 1-digit 7-segment LED, numeric LED display. Common variants: 0.28/0.36/0.39/0.56 in digit height, common anode/cathode, gray or black face, any LED color (color is a parameter only).

Gray face with white dots (Kingbright TC12-11SRWA and TC20-11SRWA datasheets state this standard for their matrices; the 8x8 variants not opened). Marking decals optional.

## Orientation Markings
Pin 1 by position at (-X,+Y). Many matrices print a dot near pin 1 (not verified).

## Recognition Features
1. 8x8 grid of round dots. 2. Square body. 3. Two 8-pin rows (16 pins). 4. Gray or black face.

## Parametric Variants
Parameters: body size (20/32), dot_dia, dot_pitch, face_color, led_color. Coupled: 7*dot_pitch + dot_dia <= body - 1.0 (4.00 pitch / 1.9 dot on 32 mm leaves 1.05 per side); row_spacing < body_x. Parameter pins in {16, 24}: 16 default; 24 only for the 58 mm Kingbright class if later confirmed.

## Recommended Base Geometry
Extruded box; array of 64 cylinders/cuts; 16 box pins.

## Modeling Procedure
1. Box. 2. Face plate inset 0.1. 3. 8x8 dot windows centered. 4. 16 pins at grid above. 5. Materials.

## LOD Strategy
LOD0: box + two pin strips. LOD1: dots as raised discs or decal grid, all pins. LOD2: dot bevels, pin shoulders.

## Simplification Rules
May omit: dot bevels, diffuser depth. NEVER omit: 8x8 dot grid, pin 1 position, 16 pins in two rows.

# [OHM-091] 16x2 LCD module
## Identity
- Canonical name: 16x2 LCD module; ID OHM-091; slug lcd_16x2
- Category: module / display; Subcategory: character LCD (HD44780-compatible 1602)
- Physical package: PKG-LCD_CHARACTER member LCM1602.std; through-hole header (16 pins) plus 4 corner mounting holes
- Aliases: 1602 LCD, LCM1602, WH1602, 16x2 character LCD. Variants: backlight color, thickness 10.0 / 13.2 / 13.5, positive/negative polarizer.
- Class D (assembly: PCB + glass stack + bezel + header + backlight), priority P1, complexity 4.

## Physical Dimensions
All from PKG-LCD_CHARACTER (Winstar WH1602 series, Vishay LCD-016N001A): PCB 80.0 x 36.0 (tol +/-0.3), module thickness 13.2 max (default; 10.0 and 13.5 variants), view area 66.0 x 16.0, active area 56.20 x 11.5, character 2.95 x 5.55 mm, character pitch 3.55 x 5.95, dot 0.55 x 0.65, dot pitch 0.60 x 0.70, 16 pins 1.0 PTH on 1.8 pads, pitch 2.54 (15 x 2.54 = 38.1), 4 holes 2.5 PTH on 5.0 pads at 75.0 x 31.0 centers. PCB thickness 1.6 (UNCERTAIN, RESEARCH_REQUIRED). Basis MFR_DATASHEET; confidence H for outline/view/active/holes (several Winstar sheets plus Vishay agree), M for thickness, L for PCB thickness, bezel, header X position.

## Geometry
Sub-bodies (Z up from PCB underside = module Z0): (1) PCB 80.0 x 36.0 x 1.6, square corners (UNCERTAIN). (2) LCD glass+polarizer+backlight stack: footprint ~71 x 25 (DERIVED, UNCERTAIN), from PCB top to 13.2 total (stack height = 13.2 - 1.6; the H2 callouts 8.6-8.9 in Vishay/Raystar sheets are unresolved). (3) Metal bezel frame, outer 70.0 x 26.0 centered (DERIVED, UNCERTAIN), window 66.0 x 16.0 centered (view area), top at 13.2; bent tabs optional (LOD2). (4) Polarizer inside the window showing 2 rows x 16 characters of 5x8 dots (decal: 2.95 x 5.55 characters, pitch 3.55 x 5.95; active area 56.20 x 11.5 centered in the window). (5) Header: 16 round pins on a single row. (6) Backlight: LED at the edge or back (pins 15, 16 = A, K); not modeled externally for the default. Reading orientation: header along the top (+Y) edge, pin 1 at the left (-X).

## Leads / Pins / Terminals
16 round pins (1.0 PTH hole per the sheets; pin dia 0.64 UNCERTAIN), pitch 2.54 along X. Pin 1 at (-19.05, 15.5) from the pin/hole bbox center, pin 16 at (+19.05, 15.5): pin row Y aligned with the mounting-hole row (hole row at +/-15.5 from center; DERIVED from the 2.5 mm callout), pin X centered (RESEARCH_REQUIRED; pin-1 offset callouts of 2.0 / 2.5 / 4.95 conflict). DEVIATION from the single-row header rule (Section 6, row along Y): the module stays in display-upright orientation with the header along X; the coordinator may rotate the footprint 90 deg if the editor requires. Pin function (VSS, VDD, V0, RS, RW, E, D0-D7, A, K) is marking only. Tail below host board -2.6 default if inserted; real tail length RESEARCH_REQUIRED.

## PCB Interface
FCO origin: center of the bbox of hole pattern (75.0 x 31.0 outer hole centers) and pins (inside it) = module PCB center (0,0). Mounting holes at (+/-37.5, +/-15.5), 2.5 PTH with 5.0 pads. Header holes 1.0 PTH, pads 1.8, pitch 2.54. Module standoff: default 0 (RESEARCH_REQUIRED; real installs use spacers or a socket); parameter standoff_mm. Body offset (0,0). Pin 1 (-19.05, +15.5).

## Materials
PCB MAT_FR4_GREEN (green most common; black/blue exist); bezel MAT_STEEL_STAINLESS (or MAT_NICKEL); glass MAT_GLASS; polarizer MAT_LCD_POLARIZER_GRAY (proposed); header pins MAT_TIN_BRIGHT; backlight diffuser MAT_PLASTIC_DIFFUSED (white); pads MAT_TIN_MATTE.

## Appearance
Typical: green PCB, silver metal bezel, gray-green STN/FSTN polarizer, or white-on-blue/black variants; characters as 2 x 16 dot cells. Varies by vendor (Winstar, Raystar, Vishay, Newhaven). Character cells are decals, separate from geometry.

## Orientation Markings
Pin 1 at the left end of the header (silkscreen '1' or square pad on some vendors, not verified here); 'A' and 'K' marks at pins 15/16 for the backlight. The display reads upright with the header at the top.

## Recognition Features
1. 80 x 36 PCB with 4 corner holes. 2. Silver bezel with 66 x 16 window. 3. 16-pin header along one long edge. 4. 2 x 16 character cells. 5. Thick body (13.2 mm).

## Parametric Variants
Parameters: thickness (10.0, 13.2, 13.5), pcb_color, bezel on/off, backlight_color, standoff_mm, polarizer tone. Coupled: bezel outer must clear the 5.0 hole pads (X < 70, Y < 26); view area stays 66.0 x 16.0 centered; active area 56.2 x 11.5 centered in the view area.

## Recommended Base Geometry
Box (PCB); box (glass/backlight stack); hollow box (bezel) with rectangular window cut; thin box (polarizer); cylinders (pins, hole rings); 32 character cells as decal or instanced dots.

## Modeling Procedure
1. PCB box with 4 holes and 16 header holes. 2. Stack box on PCB top. 3. Bezel shell with window, capped at total thickness. 4. Polarizer plane inside the window. 5. Header pins. 6. Decals: characters and silkscreen.

## LOD Strategy
LOD0: PCB box + one stack box + pin strip. LOD1: bezel window, polarizer, holes, 16 pins, active-area decal. LOD2: bezel tabs, backlight LED, glass edges, back-side COB if requested, silkscreen.

## Simplification Rules
May omit: bezel tabs, backlight LED internals, back-side parts. NEVER omit: 80 x 36 outline, four 2.5 holes at 75.0 x 31.0, 16-pin header with pin 1 side, view window 66 x 16, total thickness.

Header: black plastic housing 10.16 x 2.54 x 2.5 on the underside, 4 pins at 2.54 pitch.

4 round pins 0.64 (UNCERTAIN) on pitch 2.54 along X at Y = -12.0, X = -3.81, -1.27, +1.27, +3.81 relative to the module center. Pin 1 at (-3.81, -12.0) (the single-row header rule says along Y, but the module is kept display-upright with the header along X; DEVIATION recorded). Standoff = header housing 2.5 so the PCB underside sits at Z = 2.5.
